maps.title: Become the Disciple · Day 09 · When the Mind Says NO, Tapasya Says CONTINUE

nodeData.topic: Day 09 · When the Mind Says NO, Tapasya Says CONTINUE
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up tapah, austerity: staying fixed in one's duty while the mind pushes back, because lust, the eternal enemy, can only be conquered this way. He presents Ekadasi as the first meaning of austerity, a caring mother that shapes and polishes our lives, and answers questions on fasting beyond the body's limits and on breaking vows. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse lists the qualities a disciple learns while serving the spiritual master; yesterday covered the first, today the second. Maharaj says these qualities are not decoration but the training itself.

To be a doctor you go to medical college; to be a pilot you learn navigation at an aeronautical college. To be a good disciple we are told to develop these qualities, or we will not succeed — like a student who never gets the answer right. — “So these qualities are necessary.”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:10 (auto-transcript): “to be a doctor this qualification he must go to medical college to be a pilot he must go to aeronautical college and learn all the details about navigation and to be a good disciple”

The qualities grow by themselves as we practise, but if we deliberately work on them we move faster. That is why the Yogendras taught them to Maharaja Nimi.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:47 (auto-transcript): “they will develop as we keep practicing still, if we consciously work on these qualities It will be better. We will move faster. Therefore, they are necessary. That is why the Yujandras taught them to Maharaj Nimi and for Rosh to follow.”

Austerity means holding to one's duty while the mind throws up irrational impulses. Maharaj asks the room twice whether they understand this phrase.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:45 (auto-transcript): “So the next item is Tapaha. Tapaha or austerity means that despite the irrational impulses of the mind, one should remain fixed in executing his proper duty in life. You understand?”

children.topic: Demands last as long as the body
children.note:
While we have a body its demands for gratification continue; to transcend the body, austerity is the most important tool. Look at the Vedas and the sages — austerity is everywhere prominent.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:48 (auto-transcript): “as long as you have this body the demands for gratification will continue we transcend them we transcend the body to transcend the body austerity is most important”
Citing Bhagavad-gita 5.23, Maharaj calls this the assignment of a whole lifetime: before this body ends, the impulses must be conquered.

Rupa Gosvami's instruction is recalled: one whose senses are fully under control — held in the palm of the hand — is qualified to be a guru for the whole world.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:28 (auto-transcript): “Prabhupada Goswami mentioned this same thing The qualification for someone to become Jagat Guru is what, all the senses are under their control. In their palm. Right? It must be in our palm. Yes, especially one most controlled burning anger and the urge for one-toned sex life.”

children.topic: Human life is for Krishna consciousness
children.note:
Animals have no religion and no scripture; only humans do. So neglecting Krishna consciousness is itself a violation of human life and a very big offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:29 (auto-transcript): “So if one is not a devotee, That is, that itself is a violation of human life. It's a very big offense. Not to take to Krishna consciousness. because human form of life is meant for this so we don't see animals having religion animals don't have scripture”

children.topic: Not taking to it is offence
children.note:
Maharaj says plainly that a human being who does not practise Krishna consciousness is automatically an offender, because the human form exists for this. — “Not to take to Krishna consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 15:52 (auto-transcript): “It's a very big offense. Not to take to Krishna consciousness. because human form of life is meant for this so we don't see animals having religion animals don't have scripture only human beings have scripture so if you don't practice Krishna consciously We are offenders.”

We owe Krishna, the sages, the demigods, our parents, society and the king. Krishna consciousness is the one payment that clears every debt; otherwise we live a condemned life. — “The only way to pay is to take to Krishna consciousness.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:37 (auto-transcript): “Automatically, we are offenders. To Krishna. To the sages. To demigods. Parents. Society. The king, we are, we are debtors to all of them. The only way to pay is to take to Krishna consciousness.”

Lust, anger and greed overpower almost everyone, but devotees have the process, the knowledge and the support to conquer them. Without control we cannot be selfless, and without selflessness we cannot be good servants.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:40 (auto-transcript): “Only devotees Only devotees We have the process We have the knowledge we have the support so we can do it so this is our concern we cannot help purely if we are not selfless we cannot be a good servant”

Through Bhagavad-gita 18.45 and Bhaktivinoda Thakura, the purport teaches that one need not become a monk or a forest yogi; offering one's work to Krishna and taking shelter of the holy name brings perfection within ordinary daily life.

Maharaj recalls a great devotee's words that going off to the Himalayas to practise alone is selfish and lacks compassion. Bhaktivinoda Thakura's advice is to stay where we are and chant nicely among devotees, guided by our spiritual master.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:14 (auto-transcript): “Lord Maharaj said, going to the forest to practice with spiritual Himalayas selfishness. They are not compassionate. so Bhaktivinathakura said remain in our position and turn Hare Krishna nicely in association of devotees guided by one of our spiritual master”

Silence is one of the qualities in the verse, but our understanding of it is different from sitting quietly in a cave; it is best practised in Krishna consciousness. — “mechanical silence is useless”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:17 (auto-transcript): “so called silence silence is mentioned here as one of the qualities but our understanding of our silence is different mechanical silence is useless it is best practice in Krishna consciousness Unfortunately, if a human being neglects the regulative principles of civilized life”

Maharaj asks how many of Caitanya Mahaprabhu's followers were sannyasis. Only a handful; all the rest were householders, fully engaged and chanting, and all were successful. Our system has a perfect arrangement for everyone — we simply follow sincerely. — “It is a tested and approved method for success.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:31 (auto-transcript): “How many of his devotees are Sanyasi? Many. Disciples How many are Sanyases? Six Goswami, that is one Then They came after Before them Savadhamadha Goswami Keshava Keshava Keshava Barati Keshava Barati Paramananda Puri Paramananda Parati also”
Bhagavad-gita 3.39 calls lust the eternal enemy that covers knowledge and burns like fire. Austerity means not becoming impatient or unregulated under its waves, and those of anger and greed.

Maharaj quizzes the class. Answers come: it can never be satisfied; it is one of the three gates to hell. But anger and greed are gates too, and are not called eternal enemies — lust is singled out because it is their source.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:38 (auto-transcript): “Why loss is eternal enemy? It's our word. Do you understand it? Eternal enemy. Why is it eternal enemy? It cannot be satisfied. It cannot be satisfied. The which is Nitya Vahidana. What else? Why loss is Nitya Vahidana? One of the gates to hell. But other three are not said…”

Intelligent generals study the opponent's strength before battle; most of us want to fight without knowing what we face. On the battlefield of Kurukshetra Duryodhana pointed out to his teacher how cleverly the other side had arranged its forces.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:34 (auto-transcript): “Intelligent persons before the fight. they will check the strength of the enemy is it not they will before you fight they will spy what is the strength of the enemy most of us want to fight they don't know the strength of the enemy how do you succeed I will succeed you cannot…”

Lust is pure love of God transformed, as milk becomes yogurt: it comes from milk but can no longer act as milk. Because our love for Krishna is eternal, its perverted form is an eternal enemy while we are conditioned.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:28 (auto-transcript): “So she gave the answer. Lost is the opposite of pure love of Godhead. Pure love of Godhead is changed. Like when milk is transformed into yogurt, right? Can you remove yogurt from milk? No, it is coming from milk, but it cannot act as milk any longer because of transformation.”

Maharaj recalls the business term he was searching for: strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats. Intelligence is given to study the enemy carefully and then plan. — “we should know, then we can plan.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:04 (auto-transcript): “I remember the word I was looking for SWOT analysis SWOT analysis SWOT analysis SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT SWOT The strength, weakness, opportunity, threats, threats, threats, we should know, then we can plan.”

Having studied the enemy, the remedy is clear: austerity is not optional. Without it we cannot control ourselves or succeed.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:22 (auto-transcript): “then what's the remedy austerity is compulsory compulsory not not optional if you want to control So, austerity, austerity, without austerity, we cannot make it compulsory. So, we are looking at this, we are looking at this, we need austerity to become successful.”

Srila Prabhupada translates tapah first as fasting on certain days of the month. So when we hear the word austerity, Maharaj says, the first thing that should come to mind is Ekadasi.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:18 (auto-transcript): “So when we hear austerity, what are we talking about? What is the first thing to come to the mind? What is the first thing to come to the mind? When we hear tapah, immediately you should remember Ekadasi. They say tapahshyabhundain, that's the first one.”

Who cares for us? Ekadasi cares — she keeps us on track, fixes and polishes our lives and makes them offerable, as gold is valued only after passing through fire. — “Ekadashi shapes our lives”

🎙 Maharaj at 42:14 (auto-transcript): “Wow. Mother. Our mother. Who cares? Who cares? Ekadashi cares Mood our life Keep us on track Ekadashi shapes our lives He fixes it properly Fix our life Ekadashi polish our lives and make it offerable make it like gold gold is not appreciated”

Austerity is uncomfortable for body and mind but favourable for spiritual realisation. After an Ekadasi fast you feel happy the next day that you did it; what is very comfortable for mind and body is not where an intelligent person goes.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:44 (auto-transcript): “not comfortable for the body not shooting the mind but conducive to a spiritual realization that's austerity that is Ekadashi that shapes our lives Ekadashi gives purpose to our life in Christianity polish it”

Austerity is not for mystic power or material gain. By reducing the body's demands we clear the cloud between us and Krishna; we were expanded for his enjoyment, and by not giving it we pay heavily. — “The goal of austerity is to please Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 47:10 (auto-transcript): “Confirmed in the Bhagavatam. The goal of austerity is to please Krishna. Yes, that is the goal. I want to please Krishna.”

Animals do not work for their sense gratification, yet they get it free and without tension; we pay heavily and live in anxiety. So Krishna gives regulative principles for freedom — Ekadasi frees us and should be welcomed happily, not treated as just another day.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:41 (auto-transcript): “that we can get in the material world if you look very carefully Animals, do they work for their sanctification like human beings? Animals, do they work for their sanctification like human beings? They are getting or not? They are getting. Free.”

Maharaj stresses this is not his own recommendation: in Puri, Caitanya Mahaprabhu told the devotees not even to remember food on Ekadasi, keeping even Jagannatha's mahaprasada for the next day, and to spend the day only chanting and hearing the Bhagavatam. The devotees were happy and some went on parikrama.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:24 (auto-transcript): “This is not my recommendation. This is Chaitanya Mahabharata's recommendation. Jagannath Puri to Jagannath Pundit. Put in his book. Premi Barata. Yes, very sweet. Sweet necklace. Clearly written. It's clearly written. Chaitanya Mahabharata said. Today is a kadashi. Therefore,…”

Fasting on Ekadasi and Janmastami and keeping vows such as a householder's celibacy are devotional austerities; devotees who keep them faithfully are rarely in want. — “If you practice this nicely, you will never lack anything, materially, spiritually.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:37 (auto-transcript): “Because devotees are faithful to these practices. They rarely find themselves in a condition of want. If you practice this nicely, you will never lack anything, materially, spiritually.”

Two questions on austerity and the body, ahead of the Kartika vows.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:33 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Hare Krishna. and I feel that I can do a lot of kastriyaki. So, can I just depend on Krishna for my bodily help? Because we hear from different speakers that Krishna only protects your subtle body, not the physical body. Mataji's question is that I want to do a lot of…”

children.topic: Q1 · Fast hard and trust Krishna?
children.note:
A Mataji wants to do a lot of austerity and asks whether she can depend on Krishna for her body, since some speakers say he protects only the subtle body.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:47 (auto-transcript): “and I feel that I can do a lot of kastriyaki. So, can I just depend on Krishna for my bodily help? Because we hear from different speakers that Krishna only protects your subtle body, not the physical body. Mataji's question is that I want to do a lot of kastriyaki, and I…”

Krishna protects his devotee completely. One who practises sincerely and lives a steady life finds the material and spiritual sides balanced.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:15 (auto-transcript): “Krishna protects his devotee completely. Not so, completely. Mission and devotee sincerely practice this and really have any want.”

children.topic: Do what the body can handle
children.note:
If the body does not adjust to the austerity you want, reduce it to what it can bear. — “So we don't do things we cannot handle.”

🎙 Maharaj at 57:33 (auto-transcript): “So if the body is not adjusting to a structure as you want, so reduce it to what the body can handle. So we don't do things we cannot handle.”

children.topic: Better to leave the body fasting
children.note:
When the mind is purified one thinks: let Krishna's will be done, but this is what I will do for him — and goes ahead without missing anything. Maharaj recalls Haridasa Thakura at his departure, who could neither refuse prasadam nor take it fully, and so honoured it while continuing his fast.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:24 (auto-transcript): “When the mind has become purified to a certain stage. One would think. What Krishna wants, let it be. But this is what I want to do for Krishna. Go ahead to do it. You will not miss anything. It's better if I want to fast while living the body than to eat till they're living…”

The mind discourages us, as the gopis' parents doubted they could manage. Knowing they wanted Krishna as their husband, the gopis bathed in the cold Yamuna every winter dawn and ate saltless, spiceless khichri for a month — and on the very last day Krishna appeared.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:09 (auto-transcript): “Since our mind is not strong They want to do something Their mind will start to discourage us The gopis Were told by their parents we have never seen you do this kind of austerity before so how will you be able to do this you can't do it”

children.topic: Q2 · What if I break my vow?
children.note:
Every Kartika Maharaj is asked this before the vow has even begun. Planning for failure is very dangerous; a slip by miscalculation, followed by serious repentance, is different from searching for a loophole — Krishna cannot be cheated, only ourselves. — “we can only do that to ourselves”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:22 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, what a person who did not complete his vow. We have not started. We are already prepared for not completing. Every year I get this. I'm sure next year we'll get the same question. Very good. No, this year. I'll get the question. Means what? We are preparing to break.”

maps.title: Become the Disciple · Day 10 · A Devotee's Victory is Tolerance, Not Revenge

nodeData.topic: Day 10 · A Devotee's Victory is Tolerance, Not Revenge
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains titiksa, tolerance: the forgiving nature without which a devotee cannot preach, chant without offence or find peace. Through the tree, the cat and the dog, a slap returned, and a man who forgave a broken windscreen, he shows that tolerance spares us suffering, and in the questions he separates personal forbearance from a leader's duty to correct wrongdoing. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Today's quality from the verse is tolerance. The purport explains that a world full of irritations will infect a devotee with a spirit of revenge unless he is very forgiving.

Tolerance is praised throughout the Gita, the Bhagavatam and the Mahabharata as a quality of a sadhu. Srila Prabhupada gives two examples of it: Lord Jesus Christ and Haridasa Thakura.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:16 (auto-transcript): “Pahen Shil Describe in many places Bhagavad Gita Two Bhagavatam also Shri Mahabhatam All the qualities of a sadhu This is a tradition And the Pope and Prabhupada give an example of Lord Jesus Christ.”

Haridasa Thakura was beaten, Jesus was crucified and Nityananda Prabhu was wounded — all because they were preaching. Maharaj repeats the point in Hindi for everyone. — “One is not tolerant, one cannot preach.”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:16 (auto-transcript): “Haridash Thakur was tortured because he was preaching. This way he was crucified because he was preaching. Isai Masih ko maar diya gaya kiyo? Kiyo ki whe prachar kar raha thay. Bhagwaan Yityananda Prabhu ko bhot ghayal kar diya gaya kiyo? Whe prachar kar raha thay. One is not…”

Bhismadeva taught Maharaja Yudhisthira that forgiveness is how anger is controlled. All these qualities, Maharaj notes, are connected to one another.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:58 (auto-transcript): “One was thought is forgiving. Forgiveness, forgiveness. Which is also one of the ways to control anger. Shri Bishmadev was teaching Yudhisthira Maharaj. Shri Bishmadev was teaching Maharaj Yudhisthira to control anger, one must practice forgiveness. All these qualities, they…”

For a brahmana tolerance comes with preaching; for a kshatriya it comes with managing a movement, tolerating some disobedience and also punishing when necessary. But every devotee needs it for chanting without offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:48 (auto-transcript): “So for Brahmana, tolerance comes from preaching. For Shatriyas, the challenges of managing a preaching movement, management, if you want to be successful, tolerance is required. I have to tolerate some disobedient citizens.”

Offenceless chanting requires tolerating the senses and the mind. Maharaj warns that one who chants nicely meets more problems than others, as a reaction to that potent chanting. — “you will have more problem than others”

🎙 Maharaj at 13:13 (auto-transcript): “requires tolerance we have to treat dictated senses especially if you are chanting nicely you will have more problem than others because Because the reaction from your potent chanting.”
Referring to Bhagavad-gita 2.70, Maharaj says that whoever runs wherever the senses push can never be peaceful. To be peaceful, do not respond; keep quiet and engage more in the process.

Caitanya Mahaprabhu's example: the tree stands through wind, rain, sun and snow and remains peaceful. A devotee should be more tolerant than a tree.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:01 (auto-transcript): “For example, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu gives Chaitanya Mahaprabhu The example Chaitanya Mahaprabhu gives is the nature of the tree Chaitanya Mahaprabhu leaves branches and it leaves leaves leaves”

A tree gives fruit, shade, medicine and oxygen free, without discrimination — whoever comes may take. It is not standing for itself.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:38 (auto-transcript): “a tree gives fruit gives shade gives medicine oxygen completely free no discrimination only you can take me whoever comes take So the tree is standing not for itself.”

We mistreat the tree and it does not protest; cut down, it gives firewood for sacrifice, cooking and heating a home, and even its ashes and charcoal are useful, charcoal being part of a blood tonic. — “The tree will not stop giving service.”

🎙 Maharaj at 17:33 (auto-transcript): “Yet, we mistreated the tree. We put the tree with it. We put the tree with it. The tree will not protest. And even the tree is cut down. The tree will not stop giving service. who will continue to give service they cut down the tree they will not give you fruit but they will…”

children.topic: When to tolerate, when to act
children.note:
Mahaprabhu, who gave the tree example, also showed when tolerance applies: when his devotees were attacked, as with Nityananda Prabhu and Haridasa Thakura, he was ready to act against the offenders.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:48 (auto-transcript): “Chitanya Mahaprabhu Chitanya Mahaprabhu Vrachshaki tulna says that He taught us when to apply tolerance and win. that when there is a seal and there is no seal.”

Maharaj's simple rule: if you will not tolerate, you simply suffer; if you do not want to suffer, tolerate. Answering in kind brings the suffering home.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:11 (auto-transcript): “I will mention before tolerance if you don't want to tolerate you simply suffer if you don't want to suffer tolerate if you don't want to suffer tolerate if you want to suffer don't tolerate whatever happens”

children.topic: Slap back, end up in jail
children.note:
Someone slaps you and you slap back; he falls dead. You are not promoted to general — you are a murderer. He slapped first, but he did not kill you; now you go to jail.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:57 (auto-transcript): “Someone slap you, slap the patient back. The patient falls on dead. You get the promotion. The promotion will give you big rank. General. No, you'll be cute. They said, no, no, but he slapped me first. He slapped me to teach him a hand that I am not so cheap like that. So I…”

Or you fight back, both get wounded, and at the hospital you explain you were teaching him a lesson out of mercy, so please treat me free. The hospital agrees you are very compassionate — and hands you the bill. — “your compassion is going to pay me $10,000”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:14 (auto-transcript): “if you slap the person back he will keep quiet he will be and you had that and then wounds hospital you tell the doctor somebody slapped me and I slapped the person back because if I don't do that to the person today tomorrow we'll do the same thing to stop the person”

Krishna used the Pandavas to show us the level of tolerance through all their difficulties, and that tolerance gave them a power to control Krishna himself.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:12 (auto-transcript): “Tolerance is the quality of it, I have to think the ability, Panamanji, he was discussing with Naradamuni, He said, the Pandavas, Krishna used them to teach us the level of their tolerance, all the difficulties they passed through.”

Krishna, their messenger and Arjuna's chariot driver, wanted to return to Dvaraka; asked to stay one more week, he stayed. He left the sages meditating on him in the forest for years and forgot his own city to live with Yudhisthira. — “That is the level of Pandavas.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:29 (auto-transcript): “The Pandavas met Krishna, their messenger, see not, they met Krishna, their saraband, driving Arjuna's child who was 18 days, they detained Krishna, the mother was detained Krishna the Krishna wanted to go to Dwaraka you just said Maharaj can you stay for one more week what…”

Because people today cannot control mind and senses or tell body from soul, they become intolerant at small inconveniences. If we want real convenience, Maharaj says, we must first control the senses.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:36 (auto-transcript): “The inability of people in this age to control their mind and senses. To understand the workings of nature's laws. and to know the difference between body and soul means that they become intolerant at the slightest inconvenience we become intolerant of our senses”

A cat sees something, closes its eyes and stays peaceful; a dog sees the same thing and barks and runs about in anxiety. Tolerance brings peace.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:12 (auto-transcript): “a cat cats see something to close his eyes remain peaceful a dog see the same thing is that peaceful Patting means what? Restless, anxiety, tension. But the cat is peaceful. Peaceful. He saw it. He closes his eyes.”

Devotees learn these qualities from scripture, take them in and finally realise them, while life itself supplies plenty of practice. Prahlada Maharaja tolerated his father, and children taught tolerance early are equipped for spiritual progress.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:30 (auto-transcript): “Yes. For the reason, the voters need to regularly study these practices from scripture. Then I simulate and finally realize them. Meanwhile, both the execution of devotional service and residence in this material world offers plenty of opportunity to practice facing dualities…”

Tolerate the senses, the mind, the body's demands and others, who act differently according to the modes controlling them — and tolerate Krishna, waiting for his mercy without questioning; then he helps us succeed. — “we have to tolerate Lord Krishna”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:11 (auto-transcript): “To tolerate the senses, tolerate the mind, tolerate the body's demands, tolerate others, understand that we are of different nature we are going to act differently based on the mood which is controlling us we have to tolerate Lord Krishna”

Three questions: the consciousness behind tolerance, a leader's duty to correct, and how pure devotees train their disciples.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:23 (auto-transcript): “comment, question, questions yes want to tolerate or not okay thank you No, I cannot take it anymore. It is too much of you. I've been tolerating for all these years. Today, I can't take it. It's too much. How long will I continue like this? This is nonsense. Thank you.”

children.topic: Q1 · What consciousness makes tolerance devotional?
children.note:
The Pandavas tolerated, but so do yogis in the forest. With what consciousness should a devotee forgive — by giving the benefit of the doubt, or by accepting how the person is?

🎙 Maharaj at 36:15 (auto-transcript): “When you are saying more pandas, they were tolerating. And then they did it in Krishna. So I was thinking even the UBs who were meditating in the forest of the UBs, they were also tolerating. So I think that it's not only tolerance, it's the consciousness of how you are…”

From scripture we know that what happens to us is merited; the other person is only an instrument and I am the cause of my suffering. — “This knowledge helps one to tolerate.”

🎙 Maharaj at 38:19 (auto-transcript): “It means that I have the knowledge from the scripture that what is happening to me, I merit it. This person is acting as an instrument.”

Before coming to Krishna consciousness Maharaj saw a madman smash a man's windscreen. Guards were beating him, but the owner said let him go: in a past life I broke his, and now my karma has left me. Moved, Maharaj joined the same mystical order before finding the temple nearby.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:34 (auto-transcript): “I mentioned before, what took me to join one mystical organization, Roshikurshan Order. Roshikurshan Order. A madman broke his windscreen. The security guards were beating the man. But the man told him to leave him. I was watching the scene.”

children.topic: A sadhu should not add karma
children.note:
Knowing we are responsible makes us peaceful, like the cat rather than the dog. A sadhu does not increase his karma by answering people in the same way they treat him.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:11 (auto-transcript): “So when one knows, I am responsible for what is happening to me. You'll be happy. I'll be happy. Because as the Bhakti Dhanas is what Takurupa always said, a sadhu should not increase his karma. Sadhu should tolerate. Don't respond the same way when then people will treat us.…”

children.topic: Q2 · When should a leader correct?
children.note:
If a leader keeps silent and accepts everything as karma, will a culture of misbehaviour grow? How much should be accepted, and when should one act?

🎙 Maharaj at 45:02 (auto-transcript): “I was trying to understand, in continuation, the question, when this quality comes to that of the leaders, you mentioned we should know how to tolerate and then to punish. Here you brought in a point that we should always know that the way certain people are believing is…”

children.topic: Insults to you, insults to devotees
children.note:
If someone insults you, tolerate it; if he insults a devotee, correct it. Not correcting sends the message to the whole community that anyone may be insulted, while correction sends the opposite message.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:26 (auto-transcript): “Devotee, he sought another devotee. and you have seen it you correct it if the person insult you you tolerate it if he is a salt or a devotee you correct it if you don't correct it you have sent a message to the whole community that in this community”

Maharaj has seen leaders in bad health because they did not respond to wrongdoing. Correct it and Krishna protects you; neglect it and you are not representing him. That neglect is not tolerance. If it is beyond you, take it higher. — “take it to the appropriate quarters”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:01 (auto-transcript): “that will pollute that environment I've seen some of our leaders in a very bad health because they don't respond to wrongdoings when they're supposed to When you do it, they didn't correct it, it's affecting the health.”

When his devotees were attacked, Caitanya Mahaprabhu did not say, never mind, these things happen while preaching, you are not the body. He acted, and so should we. Slights to oneself because of one's position, though, can be let go.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:56 (auto-transcript): “honest means we are giving to wrongdoers we gave an example of Chaitanya Mahabhu he didn't come and tell the time oh I'm very sorry for this just forgive them they're useless he didn't do that you know these are the things expected while you are preaching you know just to…”

children.topic: Q3 · Do pure devotees correct indirectly?
children.note:
Pure devotees sometimes seem not to punish outright but to correct in other ways — even by glorifying the person in front of everyone. What is in their mind?

🎙 Maharaj at 53:01 (auto-transcript): “he fell down. So when I see the feelings of pure devotees, sometimes it's not just they would straight away give the punishment or give it outrightly, but there might be other ways. So even in a related discussion, I can understand by glorifying that devotee in front of…”

Maharaj's Gurudev gave some disciples the sannyasa cloth but told them not to wear it yet; he praised another as the best president, and that disciple simply enjoyed the praise. Each was a test, and none is promoted without passing. — “A teacher who does not give test is not a good teacher.”

🎙 Maharaj at 55:36 (auto-transcript): “So, when he was glorifying his devotee, when I fluttered him, he gave him a chance. He demonstrated how you are the best president. He didn't face it properly. But he was simply enjoying the, he didn't remember that the sita is on there.”

A godbrother who was corrected and given other service asked instead to go to India to be purified; Gurudev said, take my blessings. Maharaj told him the real blessing was the first instruction. He went, stayed a year, returned to Nigeria and left the movement.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:03 (auto-transcript): “One of the God brothers. He did something wrong, and Gurudev punished him, and he gave me a different service. See, he went and told Gurudev, Gurudev, now I am contaminated, so I want to go to India, Instead of the service you give to me, I want to go to India to get…”

maps.title: Become the Disciple · Day 11 · Gossip: The Silent Killer of Devotional Strength

nodeData.topic: Day 11 · Gossip: The Silent Killer of Devotional Strength
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj explains mauna, silence, not as an empty mouth but as speaking only of Krishna, which brings gravity, respect and control of the other senses. He warns that gossip, in its old village form and its new electronic form, drains our spiritual strength and our japa, and answers questions on people who interrupt japa and on sharing spiritual experiences. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Today's quality from the verse is silence. The purport explains it as avoiding worthless talk and speaking instead of what really matters — going back to Godhead.

children.topic: Not the silence of a stone
children.note:
Sitting empty-headed is not silence. Srila Prabhupada's meaning is to speak about Krishna twenty-four hours a day — that is perfect silence.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:14 (auto-transcript): “That is no silence. That is not silence. Silence is different. This Shilupapa said that silence me to speak about Krishna 24 hours. Talking about Krishna throughout.”

children.topic: We speak mostly in the mind
children.note:
Closing the mouth does not stop speech; most of our speaking happens mentally, and the quality of those thoughts implicates us and shows what we really are. — “actually we speak mentally more than vocally”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:03 (auto-transcript): “it is silence perfect silence even if we don't speak vocally we are going to speak mentally actually we speak mentally more than vocally to physically close one's mouth doesn't mean one is not speaking we are always speaking 80% of our speech is not vocal”

Because a devotee speaks only of Krishna, he has no time for nonsense. Those who chant constantly, their minds absorbed in Krishna, are practising silence in the best way.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:32 (auto-transcript): “So a devotee speaks only about Krishna. That is positive. And because he's speaking about Krishna he's not speaking about nonsensical things. It is the best practice of silence. It's a verse quoted here from Srimad Bhagavatam. If I'm not mistaken, it's from 1st counter,…”

A vow never to talk is impossible, since the mind talks constantly. The real rule is simpler: if you have nothing of Krishna to say, keep quiet and let those who know speak.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:09 (auto-transcript): “We already mentioned It's not possible. We are talking in the mind. Always we are talking. The mind is talking constantly. So there's no question of being silent. All together. And that is suitable for those who have nothing sensible to speak about. if you have nothing…”

Talk that is not about Krishna is like a frog croaking — it only announces dinner to the snake, which comes and eats it. Better to be quiet and hear from those with something to tell us. — “My dear snake, you're hungry, I'm here.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:28 (auto-transcript): “if we are not going to talk about Krishna and we are talking we are talking like a croc The cocking of a frog. The frog is cocking. But what is the benefit of that? The benefit is inviting a snake for fish. My dear snake, you're hungry, I'm here. Your food is available.”

The essence of silence is control of speech, which for devotees means avoiding idle talk and gossip. Gossip has a powerful negative effect and leaves one spiritually dry.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:43 (auto-transcript): “However, the essence of Mauna is control of speech. And for devotees that, that means avoiding frivolous talk or gossip. I am talking about Krishna only. That is the perfection of remaining silent. Talk only about Krishna. we have discussed many times”

A car with a flat tyre cannot move; those who spend their time gossiping make no spiritual advancement because they are depleted. — “Gossipers cannot make advancement.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:06 (auto-transcript): “we give example if you have a flat tire you cannot move meaning meaning that Those who spend their time in gossiping does not make spiritual advancement. Just like a flat tire cannot move, a car wouldn't move.”

A silent person's mind is not easily read; that is gravity, one of the twenty-six qualities of a devotee, and it grows from not gossiping and speaking only of Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:05 (auto-transcript): “The effect was so silent is that others cannot readily know what is on one's mind. mind that is the definition of gravity gravity is developed by silence Salim means we are not talking, we are not gossiping, no idle talks, only about Krishna.”

Gravity is a spiritually developed mind that clearly sees right and wrong and cannot be pushed about. Maharaj recalls a devotee whose idea of gravity Srila Prabhupada corrected: it is not an outward pose.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:17 (auto-transcript): “Gravity. Gravity means what? The mind is developed spiritually. One can clearly distinguish what is wrong, what is right. There is no question of being pushed. One devotee is beating gravity Prabhupada said, what is that?”

Silence is the key to secrecy. Grave people are hard to read, while speaking reveals what is in the mind; and when such a person does speak, the words land like a thunderbolt. Krishna says that among secret things he is silence.

If you really want to control your speech, study and recite the Vedas; one so absorbed never speaks nonsense, develops gravity and speaks with potency.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:55 (auto-transcript): “If you want to really control the speech study the Vedas study the Vedas recite the Vedas who can never speak nonsense It will develop gravity. It will be potency. In one speech, it will be potency.”

Speech and taste both depend on the tongue. Control speaking and eating comes under control; control eating and the other senses follow.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:12 (auto-transcript): “Additionally, because both speech and taste are dependent on the tongue, they are interrelated. Devotees must therefore control their speaking habit, speaking habit, in order to control their eating habit.”

Like celibacy, silence is taken as a vow of self-discipline: speak only of things related to Krishna, directly or indirectly. Since everything comes from the mind, the mind must be controlled. — “the mind has to be controlled.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:18 (auto-transcript): “We are accepting a self-composed vow, self-composed vow. Self-discipline. There is no secret what such a vow will entail.”

children.topic: Association of the Lord in study
children.note:
Deep study of scripture is very powerful because one has the direct association of the Lord and all the acaryas; the senses become absorbed in Krishna and one grows mindful of everything one does.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:11 (auto-transcript): “it is very powerful to study the scriptures deeply Very powerful, very powerful, because one is having direct association of the Lord, and all Acharyas, so the senses are fully absorbed in Krishna, One becomes mindful of everything that we do.”

People who talk constantly about everything but Krishna may entertain for a while, but cultured and mature people never respect them. A silent person is respected.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:51 (auto-transcript): “Those who are always talking, talking, talking, not about Krishna, but about something else. They have no respect anywhere. Cultural people, devotees, mature people, they will never have respect for such people. A silent person is always respected.”

Students begged their master to speak to them all the time. He replied that he is talking every day and only sometimes gives a discourse — his daily life is the preaching. That is silence and gravity.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:46 (auto-transcript): “One experienced Christian, One of his students asked him, Dear Master, we always want you to preach, but you don't always speak with us, we want you to speak all the time, but you are not doing that, Can you always speak to us? So he said, I am always talking.”

Krishnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami describes the eloquent speaker as one who speaks concisely, about what benefits the whole world. The topic and object of our talk must be Krishna; that is a powerful austerity.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:28 (auto-transcript): “And Krishna Dasgavra Goswami said he's an eloquent speaker. Eloquent speaker. Who speak concisely. Spoken consciously is eloquence. So the topic of discussion and the object of discussion must be Krishna.”

Ask what we are discussing, about whom, and what we hope to gain. Talk of Krishna is different: you are never tired, and the more you speak the more strength you get. — “speak about Krishna the whole day”

🎙 Maharaj at 40:16 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, we should consider what is the topic of our discussion. We must consider that. what is the topic of our discussion and we are talking about who what do we hope to gain speak about Krishna the whole day you'll never be tired the more you talk the more strength…”

The highest form of speech is sankirtan: chanting and speaking of Krishna liberates, purifies the heart and makes one hungry for more sankirtan.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:15 (auto-transcript): “Indeed, the best form of speech is Sankirtan. talking about Krishna I was chanting his names that form of speech not only liberates but purifies the heart and makes one addicted to further Sankirtan.”

Maharaj recites Caitanya Mahaprabhu's famous instructions to Raghunatha dasa Gosvami — avoid ordinary talk and its hearing, simple food and dress, give respect without seeking it, chant constantly and serve Radha and Krishna within — and calls this real mauna.

Guarding against gossip begins with caution in what we hear. Village talk today is debate about sports, politics and the weather — which party will win, whether India will beat South Africa.

🎙 Maharaj at 45:13 (auto-transcript): “Gossip idol talks It begins by exercising caution in hearing village talk. To be concise that means gossip. Village talk is gossip. Listen.”

Radio, internet surfing, television, films and forwarding their content are gossip in electronic form — very prominent and very destructive.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:31 (auto-transcript): “Electronic Gossip Very prominent Very destructive What is affecting devotees Japa the most? What is affecting devotees Japa the most? Internet, shopping, mobile, till one o'clock.”

Maharaj asks what most damages devotees' japa: internet, shopping, the phone till one in the morning. That kills brahma-muhurta, and with it we reject Krishna's invitation and shrink our own fortune. — “Yes, electronic media is destructive association.”

🎙 Maharaj at 49:02 (auto-transcript): “Internet, shopping, mobile, till one o'clock. And what is it we are looking at? Hainam, Sankirtan, Dhatayatra, Faisal. Saying get a vacation. That destroy our Brahma Mughurta.”

Gossip drains our spiritual account until even a devotee can go bankrupt. From his music days Maharaj recalls a famous American singer of the 1960s ruined by drugs and debt, whose dubious comeback ended when his own father shot him. Unlike the Avanti brahmana, he could not take his fall as a chance to turn to God.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:31 (auto-transcript): “GOSHIP DEBLETING OUR SPIRITUAL BANK ACCOUNTS Bolognians can become bankrupt it has happened in an year becoming bankrupt because I'm from music I can tell you music set”

We come to the guru to hear and then live what we hear. Why leave home only to sleep in class? Maharaj recalls a devotee who pushed through a packed hall, sat in front of senior sannyasis and then took a phone call in full view.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:43 (auto-transcript): “She does not just hear these things. She does not just hear these things. She does not just hear them. Practice them. Then it will become a reality. That is what we want. We want to experience what we are hearing from the scriptures. we just waste our time come and sit with…”

Two questions: people who want to talk during japa, and whether to share spiritual experiences.

🎙 Maharaj at 61:28 (auto-transcript): “Comment. Do you think I'm going to take it for you? Take it for you to do it. So my question is, sometimes when I'm practicing, you know, genuinely, seriously, when you're signing, but someone comes and they find you is not good and they want to speak with me or something. So…”

children.topic: Q1 · Someone talks during my japa
children.note:
When I chant seriously, someone comes to talk; I compromise so as not to alienate them, but my focus goes. What is the right approach?

🎙 Maharaj at 61:38 (auto-transcript): “So my question is, sometimes when I'm practicing, you know, genuinely, seriously, when you're signing, but someone comes and they find you is not good and they want to speak with me or something. So you feel, okay, maybe you are going to accommodate them and loosen up a…”

For one who really wants to chant, a person who distracts from japa is an enemy, however important the talk is made to seem. — “a friend will encourage you to chant”

🎙 Maharaj at 63:00 (auto-transcript): “That's an enemy, for one who really wants to chant, it's an enemy, to declare it very clearly, It's not a friend, a friend will encourage you to chant, and then they want to distract you from chant. Yes, I wondered what he was asking me a question, but he was very clever.”

children.topic: So what if they call you proud?
children.note:
Of billions on the planet, how many chant Hare Krishna? Even chanting mechanically, you have begun the journey. And whatever you do, some will still call you proud.

🎙 Maharaj at 64:14 (auto-transcript): “if I don't discuss the person is going to say I'm proud and then what if you are proud then what so what yes I should be proud that I'm chanting Harkis how many people have chant Harkis in this world how many people I would talk to 2 million even we have to 1 billion 10…”

Time for japa, give attention to japa; time for Bhagavatam, hear it; time for prasadam, sleep or service, do that. Srila Prabhupada designed it; the scripture is clear until we bring our crookedness into it. — “Don't mix everything up.”

🎙 Maharaj at 66:23 (auto-transcript): “This is the time I pray. Yes. Time for Japa. Give attention to Japa. Time for Bhagavatam. Hear Bhagavatam. Time for Prasadam. Take Prasad. Time for sleep. Time for other services. Do their services. Papa designed all these things. We should just follow it. Don't mix…”

children.topic: Q2 · Share realisations or keep them?
children.note:
Does sharing a spiritual experience dilute it, and does keeping it inside make it stronger?

🎙 Maharaj at 68:10 (auto-transcript): “I was thinking about this earlier today. When we have certain experiences in our devotional time or some specific locations, so one tendency is to share it with our peers, our friends and feel happy about it that I've experienced something. And the other is we keep it within.…”

Some things are only for a certain class of people. Tell friends you danced with Krishna all night and they will call it a joke. There is even a principle for dreams: told at once, a good dream is neutralised and turns into pride.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:46 (auto-transcript): “There are certain things which are called confidential. It is for a certain class of people. If you tell your friends, this night I will dancing with Krishna this night”

Days before leaving, Maharaj's spiritual master hesitated over whether revealing a confidence might be pride. People are envious, even our closest friends; some things may be said, but look at whom you are telling.

🎙 Maharaj at 72:29 (auto-transcript): “there is a principle she didn't share it immediately If you see a dream immediately, you neutralize the good one, you neutralize everything. It becomes like a pride. I remember my special master said, I don't know whether I should say this, would it be a pride or not? When he…”

maps.title: Become the Disciple · Day 12 · Not Reading the Scriptures is Also an Offence

nodeData.topic: Day 12 · Not Reading the Scriptures is Also an Offence
nodeData.note: SB 11.3.24 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj takes up svadhyaya, study of scripture: Srila Prabhupada's books gather all the acaryas in one place, and studying them fills the heart with determination to serve, while neglecting them is an offence. Through Visvarupa and the boy Nimai he shows what real study does, urges devotees to learn mantras and feast daily on the scriptures, and answers questions on why the desire to serve changes, on knowledge versus information, and on finding time to study. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Today's quality from the verse is study of Vedic literature, each according to his ability, and teaching others. The purport points especially to Srila Prabhupada's books.

children.topic: All the acaryas in Prabhupada's books
children.note:
Bhagavatam, Bhagavad-gita, Nectar of Instruction, Nectar of Devotion, Caitanya-caritamrta: Srila Prabhupada collected the commentaries and realisations of all our acaryas into them, so reading his books carefully is reading theirs. — “All these books have everything you need to become Krishna conscious.”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:12 (auto-transcript): “We have so many books given by Siddha Prabhupada. Principally, we are studying Bhagavatam, Bhagavad Gita, Lecture of Instruction, Lecture of Devotion, Siddha Prabhupada, Chaitan Chaita Tambrit. All this Prabhupada has given to us. Shri Chaitanya Mahabharata. All these books…”

Rather than spend time on activities that destroy bhakti, engage in these books — not to become a scholar but to become Krishna conscious. — “The intention is not to become a big scholar.”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:31 (auto-transcript): “instead of wasting our time for unnecessary activities that would destroy our bhakti. Better to engage ourselves in these books. The intention is not to become a big scholar. Studying the Vedas helps to control our speech.”

Study controls speech and the tongue and builds love for Krishna, because his qualities are clearly described. Reading the Tenth Canto, the mind naturally goes to Krishna's activities.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:03 (auto-transcript): “Studying the Vedas helps to control our speech. It will control our tongue. It will help us to develop love for Krishna. because Krishna's qualities are clearly defined. When you look at the 10th kanto of Bhagavatam,”

If we do not read the scriptures we offend them, disregard Srila Prabhupada's instructions and deny ourselves what the acaryas laboured to give us.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:30 (auto-transcript): “So we discussed the other day if we don't read our scriptures we are naturally offenders. We are offending the scriptures. breaking the destructions for Srila Prabhupada we deny ourselves to the massive of acharyas because they spend their time nectar of devotion Srila…”

One studies two hours, another thirty minutes, another an hour — according to schedule and according to desire. Everyone should engage.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:58 (auto-transcript): “So I couldn't have our ability to study them. Someone may study for two hours. Someone has 30 minutes. Someone, maybe one hour. According to our schedule, or base our desire. According to our desire. We should engage ourselves. It is said here, one becomes a few words, the…”

In a civilised society children began study at five. Studying the Vedas from childhood gives a solid foundation, so one already knows what to do and what to expect in life.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:44 (auto-transcript): “So, in a civilized age, at the age of five, five, children are sent to Gurkul. For what? For what? to study initiated into study. That is a foundation for our life.”

Maharaj dwells on a phrase from the purport: proper study creates courage and determination in the heart to serve the Lord, and leaves no determination for sense gratification. He calls it a very powerful word.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:10 (auto-transcript): “When you study the scripture very nicely. Do you know? I'm looking at this word very carefully. what becomes infused with a static determinist one to serve the supreme prestige of Godhead is his courage from studying the scriptures determination is created in the heart…”

Saci-mata's elder son Visvarupa studied the Vedas under Advaita Acarya, lost interest in everything else and left home to serve the Lord.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:06 (auto-transcript): “Sachi Mata She said My son What's your name? Vishwarup. Study the Vedas under Dvita Acharya. What happened? What happened? One becomes in fear with determination to serve the”
Study has two possible effects depending on our motive. Studied properly it makes one naturally humble, as Bhagavad-gita 5.18 describes; studied with another desire it makes one proud.

As one flushes stool without a second look, real study throws out material desire as trash. Nobody wants to inspect yesterday's gulab jamuns, rasagullas and pizzas. — “This is what happens when one study the Vedas properly.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:29 (auto-transcript): “Exactly like when one passes stool, what do you do? Flush it, right? Exactly. This is what happens when one study the Vedas properly. Material desire, completely thrown out. Oh, this is trash. Not even second. Yesterday, I took gulab jamons, rasa gulabs, and sundaes,”

Fearing Nimai would leave like his brother, Jagannatha Misra stopped his studies, saying Krishna, not education, maintains us. Nimai sat on discarded cooking pots and would not come down, arguing that if all is earth, food and pots are the same; when Saci-mata explained the difference, he asked how he could learn such things without school — and was allowed back. He needed no study, but was teaching us that we do.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:04 (auto-transcript): “was not happy were that then when Jagannam Srta. Chita Mahaprabhu was addicted also in his study they said Disharupa, he lived after stuttering the Vedas. We could tolerate it because we have the face of Nimai Pandit to look at. Now he is stuttering the Vedas too scrutinizingly.”

Study is not just reading; it becomes absorption. To be 'infused' means Krishna's energy enters and spreads through our consciousness. In Prabhupada's books Svarupa Damodara, Raghunatha, Rupa, Sanatana, Jiva and many others are all in one place, and material desire quietly goes away. — “So studying the Vedas is association with Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:45 (auto-transcript): “This is study. Not just reading. You study. Look at the word carefully. that becomes absorption the absorption is Krishna consciousness one becomes infused means what the energy from Krishna is entering into us spread through all our consciousness Krishna consciousness…”

We eat with the tongue; we should also feed it with Krishna's glories. Srila Prabhupada recommended every devotee learn to chant mantras, because they will save us at death.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:10 (auto-transcript): “This is the story of the Great House. This compulsory we eat with the tongue we should eat also by chanting the glories of Krishna vibrating these mantras. Lepapa recommended every devotee should learn chanting mantras because it will save us at the time of death.”

As an elephant Gajendra chanted no new mantras; he remembered prayers learned as a king in his previous life, and Krishna appeared.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:57 (auto-transcript): “He was speaking because of Gajendra. Gajendra chanted the mantra he learned from past life. Not the present life. the person as an animal he didn't chant mantras the previous life as a king he chanted many mantras that helped him in the next life but he chanted the mantras he…”

The Bhagavatam, the Gita, the Siksastaka, the Brahma-samhita, the Nrsimha-kavaca, the Radha-krpa-kataksa — so many. Engaged in them we are automatically saved from prajalpa, and at japa the mind stays with the mantra.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:51 (auto-transcript): “There are so many mantras in Bhagavatam. Bhagavad Gita, lots of instructions, Shri Shokamishar, tend to come to so many mantras. Brahma Samitai says, Shri Satsakam is said, So many. The Sengha Kavachar is there. So many. Radha Kripa Kutakshar is there. So many. Let's engage…”

During a month-long observance many devotees found themselves chanting the prayers in their dreams. If one month does that, why not a lifetime? Maharaj's answer: laziness — give it up. — “how we are cheating ourselves”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:56 (auto-transcript): “last time when we were observing Gorshatan Ma for one month just for one month many devotees confess as the mantra was chanting they continue to chant them in their dream that is for one month for a lifetime can we see how we are cheating ourselves can we see we are cheating…”

The scriptures say get up — get up and see the feast waiting. If we do not feast on them we stay hungry and eat prajalpa instead; we must eat something, so eat what has been given. — “We should eat what is proper”

🎙 Maharaj at 37:16 (auto-transcript): “so in the scripture you will hear get up get up means what to study the scriptures to study the scriptures yes get up look at the scriptures see what is available see what is waiting for us feast we have feast right we have lot of feast let us feast everyday if you don't…”

The Gosvamis wrote every day here in Vrindavan. You cannot write without thinking, just as you cannot phone someone without thinking of them; absorbed in Krishna, they wrote it down for us. Not studying disobeys the acaryas.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:35 (auto-transcript): “This is what the Goswami's were doing every day here. Every day they are busy writing. You cannot write something you are not chanting. Before you write something you are thinking about it. Right? Just like before you call somebody, you are thinking about that person. You…”

Not speculation or reading for prestige. Maharaj asks the sign of knowledge: humility, and renunciation — everything else becomes trash because one is nourished by Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:53 (auto-transcript): “What is the sign that one has knowledge? We already mentioned one thing, one becomes very humble. What is the sign that one has knowledge? What is the sign that this person is knowledgeable. What do you see in the person that has knowledge, qualities? The person is renounced.…”

Looking through the Sixth Canto the day before, Maharaj laughed to see how much nectar is inside while we do not eat it. Please don't starve — eat.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:51 (auto-transcript): “I was laughing yesterday when I was looking at the Ciscanto and the nectar was there I was looking and see how we are cheating ourselves so much nectar is inside we are not eating please don't starve yourself eat eat Hare Krishna make comments”

Three questions: the changing motive for study, knowledge versus information, and householders with no time.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:35 (auto-transcript): “make comments questions yes in the beginning we all have a desire to practice the host and service in the same way then let me I see some of what happens When he starts writing scriptures with that desire, I don't know at what point that desire starts shaping that it becomes…”

children.topic: Q1 · Why does the motive change?
children.note:
We begin studying to serve, but at some point the desire turns to scholarship and speaking for recognition. When and why does it change?

🎙 Maharaj at 42:43 (auto-transcript): “in the beginning we all have a desire to practice the host and service in the same way then let me I see some of what happens When he starts writing scriptures with that desire, I don't know at what point that desire starts shaping that it becomes now more inclined to become…”

A subtle hidden desire must first be cleared. Krishna knows us better than we do, yet asks: is it me you are looking for in the scriptures, or something else? He tests us so that we define where we belong. — “Krishna wants you to decide.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:20 (auto-transcript): “When we studied the scripture, just like anything else we want to do, The result, there is the result to come out. First of all, we have to get the subtle desire which I've been hiding there cleared. We should always be conscious”

Sarasvati told Kesava Kasmiri that the mantra she gave him was for Krishna consciousness, not to make him a conquering scholar — but he changed. Scripture can become entertainment for the intellect.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:10 (auto-transcript): “Saraswati told Kisawa Kasmiri, the purpose of the mantra I gave you is not to become a Dig Vijay. That was not the reason. I gave you for Krishna consciousness but you changed. So Krishna wants to he wants us to clearly define where we are. So he made the test.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments on Sukadeva's phrase. Praised all day as a great prabhu, a devotee starts to believe it; the fortunate one is shaken, sees what he has become and takes shelter of Krishna. That fear is the turning point.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:24 (auto-transcript): “Shilabhishwana Chakrabhati Takwala explains that Sukadev Goswami used the word fear of cancer. Fear of kamsa. Sukhadev Goswami used the word boldly in the Bhagavata. Vishnu Takvati gave purport to that. What is fear of kamsa? In one Dhammaswami lecture, I say fear of kamsa is…”

Gour Govinda Maharaj lamented that sincere newcomers become politicians after some years. A service given becomes a position — dangerous; the fortunate humble themselves and return to bhakti. — “we came here as sincere boys and girls.”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:08 (auto-transcript): “They will continue. As Srila Gurguvina Maharaj said, we came here as sincere boys and girls. After some years, after some years, now we are politicians, no more devotees. One who is fortunate at the point, see what I'm doing. I mean persecuted by a position instead of…”

Position-seekers meet, rest and eat but do not chant; the fortunate find someone to tell them they have become a boss. A senior sannyasi once proposed going to Jagannatha temple to dance and then to the Ganga instead of a meeting. Maharaj has seen devotees leave their bodies lamenting what they leave behind — so take sadhana seriously now.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:55 (auto-transcript): “You see, many so-called sino devotees want a position they are not chanting the Japa. Eating throughout the whole day and night. They are meeting, they are resting or eating. So how will they change? Those who are fortunate, they will get somebody who will tell them, you are…”

A question about understanding the mahajanas and the true objective of knowledge.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:27 (auto-transcript): “It's a great question. Its question is, the question of knowledge should be the objective of knowing. Today, knowledge is a little bit. We need to make a bug also. We will go to google and check how it works. If you go to Google and get a recipe, you start to prepare some things.”

Finding a recipe on Google and never cooking it is just information; reading books in detail without application is the same. Applied knowledge becomes realisation — as they say in West Africa, half knowledge is dangerous. — “it is not knowledge, it's an information.”

🎙 Maharaj at 58:48 (auto-transcript): “We will go to google and check how it works. If you go to Google and get a recipe, you start to prepare some things. But you don't practice it. What is that? It's just information. It has no value.”

Who decides who worships the deity, cooks or does sankirtan? It is already within us, and a guru once revealed it early. Today a born businessman is sent to be an aeronautical engineer and called dull; placed where his nature lies, he rises at once.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:48 (auto-transcript): “So who decides who should do deity worship, who should do pujas, who should do cooking, who should do sankitan, who should do, who decides? It is already inside us. We came with these things. So when we are sent to the Guru in the beginning all these things are taught.”

Householders must work hard for years before they have time to study deeply. How can they avoid lamenting and still serve?

🎙 Maharaj at 63:13 (auto-transcript): “The question says, Griyastas, we need to study and work hard in fields of avidya for several years at the beginning of their career before they finally gain substantial time to dwell very deeply to Vedang and Shastras. Since such Shastrit study requires considerably cognitive…”

We have twenty-four hours; make it thirty-six and we would still have no time. The lack is interest — with interest, time appears, and what we like feels simple.

🎙 Maharaj at 64:28 (auto-transcript): “First of all, It is not because you don't have time. We don't have interest. We have 24 hours. So Christians should make it 36. Even if Christians make it 36, we still have no time. But if we have interest, we will have time. so the things we don't like they are difficult…”
Even without an appetite for reading one can hear: everything is now on the phone, in every language. Krishna says those who worship after hearing from others also cross beyond birth and death.
