maps.title: Radha Sunya · Session 11 · Helping Peers Instead of Criticizing

nodeData.topic: Session 11 · Helping Peers Instead of Criticizing
nodeData.note: NOI 6 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Correction belongs to superiors who act out of love; between equals the better way is to help, wait patiently for a sincere devotee who is still 'in the shower', and set the example rather than find fault. Through Haridasa Thakura, the Gosvamis and Srila Prabhupada, Maharaj shows how a sadhu raises others up, and he gives practical ways to stop critical conversations, replace criticism with prayer and fill the mind with Krishna's pastimes instead. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj restates the aim of the series: to understand how devastating aparadha is so that we can overcome it. Today's theme is how to help our peers in Krishna consciousness instead of criticizing them, since criticism usually comes from envy. Maharaj has even seen a group whose Kartik vow is to search out devotees and criticize them, while the acaryas spent their lives searching the scriptures for their essence.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:20 (auto-transcript): “What is our interest? Our interest is to help us understand how devastating and dangerous is our Radha so that we can overcome it and all the facilities for overcoming it is all being massively presented. and I pray and beg our chariots to help us understand this and make the…”

Srila Prabhupada told a disciple that while his godbrothers praised him, Prabhupada alone kept correcting him, because that is the spiritual master's duty. Fortunate devotees are chastised and corrected; without it how would we know what to avoid?

🎙 Maharaj at 17:32 (auto-transcript): “And so the Papa told one devotee, if I remember, it was tedious. All your groupers are talking very good about you, but only me is always criticizing and criticizing you. That is my duty. That is my duty. The good brothers, God sisters, yes, they're talking good, they're…”

Superiors have our interest at heart and see our future, so they have the right to correct. Equals and juniors, still driven by mundane senses, should not take up that service; correction given in love by a superior is purifying, especially when it is accepted. — “I cannot have a disciple I cannot chastise.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:47 (auto-transcript): “Criticizing should be done by our superiors. Our superiors, they have our interest in their mind. They see our future. Therefore, they have the right to make the correction so we can make advancement. Others who are equal and junior should not do this service because our…”

Those in management can see more, so their correction, even when it looks like anger, is love. — “That anger is love.”

🎙 Maharaj at 26:23 (auto-transcript): “But those who are in the management position should see. They can see. That is why in the beginning, we started by saying that the superiors will see and make the correction because they have a better side. They have a better understanding. So their correction, even if it is…”

An inexperienced devotee placed Prabhupada's tent at the far end of the Kumbha Mela, where he could not preach, and Prabhupada rebuked him. The devotee did not justify himself but grieved over wasting his guru's time and tried to think how to set it right. Prabhupada called him back holding a closed fist; fearing a blow, the devotee came closer and found ice pressed into his hand — Prabhupada had felt his mood and reciprocated.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:02 (auto-transcript): “One day, Slappapath attended Kumbh Mera. The devotees who did the arrangement were not so experienced. So the tent he arranged for Prabhupada was at the end. At the end, when Prabhupada came, what is this? I did not come here to come and take a bath. I came here to preach and…”
Maharaj takes up a point from the Nectar of Instruction, text 6: a sincere devotee who still shows faults is like someone in the middle of a bath, in the process of becoming clean.

children.topic: Wait until the bath is over
children.note:
Pointing at soap on someone's ear while they are still bathing is not fair; check only when they have finished. Even then, correct with a smile and the wish to help, not to show superiority. Shouting from superiority affects people negatively even when we are right; correction offered to help works positively, and the Supersoul later shows even a proud person who was right.

🎙 Maharaj at 23:28 (auto-transcript): “I have not finished bathing. So if you are seeing, oh, see soap on your ear. Are you correct to say that? I have not finished bathing. You can do that only when I have finished. Then you see soap there. See, you need to check carefully. And even with that, it should be done…”

A sadhu does not excuse deviations by claiming to be a sadhu; he keeps checking where he must adjust. His remaining faults are burned up in time by the fire of bhakti, so others should be patient.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:06 (auto-transcript): “So, a sadhu is properly situated when he or she is not justifying their mistakes as a sadhu. If one is justifying their mistakes, you know, I'm a sadhu. But a sadhu would not say that anyway. A sadhu would not say that. will not say that. A sadhu will not justify his or her…”

Someone who breaks principles, steals or fights and then says 'I am a sadhu' is wrong. The sadhu is the one who slips through past conditioning, feels bad, and prays for forgiveness and correction; looking at where his practice will take him, we already see him as pure. Mistakes born of weakness are not deliberate acts, so we can overlook some things.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:04 (auto-transcript): “not that so many breaking principles stealing money and beating fighting devotees breaking people misrepresenting he says oh no no I'm a sadhu I'm a sadhu that is wrong That person cannot be a sadhu. A sadhu, when he's trying, he should have been. He's a trying. But the way…”

Anger between a devotee and authority, when excessive, easily becomes aparadha. Maharaj turns to Narottama dasa Thakura, whom a king and mayavadi brahmanas condemned for initiating brahmanas though not born one.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:47 (auto-transcript): “That is true. Just like what we see in the picture. This is anger pointing hand to, even if you look carefully, you see that the person is pointing hand to his senior. Look at the fulgence, look at the fulgence. Just like we, we see in the life of, we see in the life of…”

Like Hanuman opening his chest to show Sita and Rama, Narottama revealed an effulgent spiritual brahmana thread that eclipsed theirs, and they all accepted him as a pure devotee. Being angry with such a devotee is a very great offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:22 (auto-transcript): “Narutam Dasekura did, just like Hanuman did. When Hanuman opened his chest, what was there? Sit around. What was inside? Similarly, Narottam Dasekura opened his eyes and they were able to see a Brahman trade, very effulgence. And the effulgence of the Brahman trade, which is…”

children.topic: We see according to our level
children.note:
An external devotee cannot see another's purity; only pure devotees recognise one another, which is why they are always together in kirtan and festivals. So we must be very careful in our dealings.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:41 (auto-transcript): “So, so be careful in our dealings because we generally see things according to our level. And the external devotee is not going to see the purity of any devotee. Because he doesn't have the qualification to see. Only a pure devotee can see. Like, all these devotees who know…”

Srila Prabhupada wrote in a letter that it is better to set an example than to criticize, since members come from ordinary people and cannot be expected to meet the standard at once. Criticizing is easy; the real challenge is to improve the situation.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:20 (auto-transcript): “It's easy to criticize. Yeah, that is good. That is correct. The real challenge for us is to help improve the situation by helping in some way, especially by setting a good example ourselves. Yes, we have mentioned before that criticism is due to envy. I'm superior to you, so…”

Rupa Gosvami described Krishna's hair as like a snake; Sanatana Gosvami questioned it and Rupa kept silent, accepting him as his guru. Later Sanatana saw a snake-like shape in the water, approached and found it was only hair — and his experience confirmed the verse. This is constructive criticism that expands the pastime.

Isvara Puri asked Caitanya Mahaprabhu to check his composition. Mahaprabhu first said a pure devotee's writing has no fault, then suggested one word be adjusted; after weighing it from every side, Isvara Puri showed that his word was right, and Mahaprabhu happily accepted defeat. Such a sadhu writes not to show scholarship but because it comes from Krishna for the world's benefit.

Complaining every time that a place is dirty changes no one and only makes the other person justify himself. If I clean it every time I come, one day he will start doing the same. Criticism is the cheapest way and shows our laziness and envy; example is rare because it is high quality. — “Character is power.”

🎙 Maharaj at 47:21 (auto-transcript): “So I come here and I say, see, see, see. Every time I come here, see, see. Every time this place is so dirty. Every time like this. What is this? children.topic: A sadhu asks how to help
children.note:
Following Nityananda's approach of transforming rather than killing the Jagais and Madhais, Haridasa Thakura did not curse the woman sent to seduce him; he waited for her and raised her consciousness. — “What can I do to help?”

🎙 Maharaj at 50:47 (auto-transcript): “So Haridash Takura took risk here to help make a devotee. That is the potency of a sadhu. A sadhu will not just be going around cursing people. children.topic: She came only to bring him down
children.note:
Maharaj tells of a woman who came to his programmes for a time bringing offerings, whose real aim, like that of the woman sent to Haridasa, was to bring down religious leaders. When it did not happen she stopped coming.

children.topic: Three nights of the Holy Name
children.note:
Haridasa chanted the pure Name into her ears for three nights; she became a pure devotee, shaved her head, chanted constantly and went back to Godhead. This is a sadhu.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:02 (auto-transcript): “And Haridasa Kota knew about her coming, but he waited for her and chanted the pure name into her ears for three nights. And she became a pure devotee. Shaved her head, sat before two and chanted three thousand names like a guru and went back to Godhead. This is a sadhu. It…”

Winning arguments wastes time. Sarasvati told Kesava Kasmiri her mantra was not for defeating scholars; she could not stand before the 'small boy', Mahaprabhu, her Lord. He returned, fell flat offering obeisances, and Mahaprabhu raised and embraced him, cutting his material bondage. Helping an offender to advance helps us advance too.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:57 (auto-transcript): “heart. So, yeah, I defeat you. So, then what? Then what? Then Saraswati told Keshavaka Smiri, the mantra I gave to you, it is not for promoting your falsehood, going everywhere to defeat scholars. The mantra is to help you to become Christian conscious. But you wasted the…”

After a few minutes of journaling on what a devotee's faults reveal about us, whether we would scold a peer with a fever, and how our guru wants us to behave, devotees share their realisations. Others tell how they learned to hear correction as Krishna speaking, to pray instead of criticize, and to see that we are all the same souls living different moments.

🎙 Maharaj at 68:04 (auto-transcript): “I would like devotees to raise their hand all those who want to share their realization and already two hands are raised so first i would like to uh um that shweta mataji you can unmute yourself and share your realization my humble and respectful of our senses on to you so…”

Responding to a devotee, Maharaj agrees that what we see in others is in us. We should switch on the light in the room of our own consciousness and clear it out, rather than shine it into someone else's room. And if a peer has a fever, we take him to the clinic rather than criticize. — “What we see in others is actually in us.”

🎙 Maharaj at 70:27 (auto-transcript): “Yes, you are correct. What we see in others is actually in us. Ecclesiastes use them to show us that we have those things. So better not to look at them, but to look at ourselves. That's how we can correct us. We discussed the other day, Bhakti Bhattacharya said we should…”

A devotee who came to Krishna consciousness through rituals feels torn about criticizing them. Maharaj says people come by different ways according to their background; leave the road open, and for himself, now that he has seen the reality, simply get fixed in the practice.

🎙 Maharaj at 87:21 (auto-transcript): “i do i think this is my problem every everyone has different ways to to come to christian consciousness according to our background our nature so christian consciousness is open in different direction from different ways people get connected with christian so you go connected…”

Maya's espionage is to set devotees against each other so they lose enthusiasm for their mission. Even without offending ourselves, constantly hearing criticism weakens our creeper, so we must not stay in such conversations.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:40 (auto-transcript): “How to stop the critical conversation? If someone repeatedly tells you about their problems with another person, you have to let them know that you don't want to hear it. Prabhu, is there anything good about that person? Prabhu, how can we help this person? We should put a…”

Ask the person to share something from a lecture or reading; people are dry and have little to share, so we can bring in something nourishing. With a senior, excuse yourself: the topic is too heavy, it is time for service — but do not remain there.

🎙 Maharaj at 92:42 (auto-transcript): “You change the topic. Change the topic. Bring on something. Can you share something with me? Something you read this Monday, the lecture you attended. Can you share with me? You see, people are very addicted today. They are very dry. They will not have anything to share. So…”

An apple a day is healthy, but feasting on the forbidden apple — criticizing devotees — leaves us dead spiritually and materially. If we are busy advancing and encouraging others in their services, we have no time to watch what others are doing. Where practice is positive, the whole environment becomes charged and everyone who enters feels nourished.

🎙 Maharaj at 94:12 (auto-transcript): “What can we do to help this person? Instead of this person has a problem what can we do to help? Not to start feasting on his solenoid Radha Maharaj said feasting on forbidden apple. The water should not feast. Apple is very nice. In fact, it's recommended that once you eat…”

As a last exercise at the GBC College, students who had lived together for a year sat in a circle, each writing a few good things about every other person on a paper passed around. Meditating on those qualities purifies; meditating on garbage destroys not the other person but ourselves. — “it is ourselves that we are destroying”

🎙 Maharaj at 96:50 (auto-transcript): “And when we did, the last thing we did in the GBC College, the last exercise is all the students, everyone sits together. Those who have been seeing each other, interacting with each other for a year. So at least. And some devotees were men for many years before. So we sit in…”

children.topic: What we meditate on, we become
children.note:
After scripts for redirecting, setting boundaries and leaving, Maharaj stresses that what we contemplate constantly is our future; dwelling on people's bad deeds will never make us better.

nodeData.topic: Session 12 · Seek the Association of Devotees
nodeData.note: CC Madhya 19.156–157 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Disobeying the guru and living by one's whims is the 'mad elephant' that uproots the bhakti creeper, as Sita, Indra and Ramacandra Puri show. Because we cannot live without association and need love, we must choose the company of devotees, make that company genuinely caring, and fence our creeper. In the questions Maharaj distinguishes revealing the mind from criticism and explains what makes a first-class disciple. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
On Diwali, day 12 of the series continues to look at the devastating effect of aparadha, focusing today on how to seek the association of devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:49 (auto-transcript): “Radha Suniya, the missing link, day 12. Today, while we are trying to, trying to understand the dangerous, devastating effect of Aparada and trying to overcome it, we want to focus today particularly on how to seek the association of devotees. How to seek the association of…”
Caitanya-caritamrta compares an offence that uproots the bhakti creeper to a mad elephant; the purport links it especially to disobeying the spiritual master.

No doctor goes from house to house begging patients; people come to him. Why go to a doctor and pay him if you will not trust him or take his medicine? Coming to the guru and then rejecting his instruction is the same madness. — “that is a madness”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:03 (auto-transcript): “dry up. Why should one go to a doctor if he don't need medication? Why? Why should one go to a doctor if he don't need medication? Why should one go to a doctor if you know that it's not a quack? Why should one go there? A doctor doesn't want to come to someone's house. I'm a…”

The Gita describes one who rejects scripture and acts on whims: he attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal — three things are gone. Whimsical activity should not be offered to Krishna.

children.topic: A mad elephant in a garden
children.note:
Maharaj recalls a devotee he spoke with that afternoon who is repeating another's whimsical mistakes. Even a calm elephant ruins a garden; a mad one is worse.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:52 (auto-transcript): “A devotee is rejecting the instruction of the person, acting whimsically. It doesn't make sense at all. That's why it is described as madness. It is madness. And when a mad elephant, even if the elephant is not mad, entering a garden is devastating. And then if the elephant…”

Maricha first warned Ravana from experience not to oppose Rama, and went only when threatened with death. Lakshmana then drew a protective circle and told Sita not to step out of it.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:34 (auto-transcript): “In the forest, when the Sita Devi and Balmachanda and Lakshman were in the forest, Maricha disguised as a deer by the advice, the advice instruction, not the advice, the order of a Ravana. The first time, the first time, Ravana came to tell Marichi to disguise and deceive…”

Sita stepped out, and the result of that disobedience was a full year in captivity, harassed day and night by demons.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:00 (auto-transcript): “nothing can enter here so don't go outside stay here laxman lived and see that david suffered she was getting out what was the result of disobedience one full year suffering is longer so when we say mad elephant offense which we try to understand how devastating how…”

When Indra disrespected his spiritual master, Brihaspati hid himself even after Indra repented, so that Indra would experience the result and never repeat it. Minimizing the guru, in the mind or openly, is how a devotee destroys his own life.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:46 (auto-transcript): “What about Indra? Disrespecting his special master, Pihaspati. What happened? Devastating. Pihaspati knew Indra had repented from his offense and he was coming to beg and he hid himself. He personally did that so he could experience it. The next time you will not do that. It…”

Ramacandra Puri, a disciple of Madhavendra Puri, arrogantly corrected his own guru at the time of his passing and was sent away, while Isvara Puri served faithfully and was blessed. The spiritual master is never the object of our correction.

🎙 Maharaj at 35:16 (auto-transcript): “I wish I would have another beautiful experience Iswara Puri Ramachande Puri What did my disciple of Madhavinta Puri What did he have a relationship with Sri Chita Mahapuram Ramachande Puri was very arrogant and he was correcting and advising his Bursha master very dangerous…”

Later Ramacandra Puri found fault with Mahaprabhu himself — ants on the sweets, a sannyasi eating too much. Mahaprabhu had Govinda announce that no one should invite him for prasada, and the devotees were shocked to learn why.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:56 (auto-transcript): “you are a sanyasi see ants there are ants everywhere everywhere there are ants but a fault finder will not see ants anywhere. You will not see eat what a sanyasi you are eating sweet ants Sweet. You, Sanyasi. You. Oh, the full course is meant for 10 people you have eaten in.…”

Maharaj says it is a hundred times better to be struck by an atomic bomb or burnt in fire than to be abandoned by Vaishnavas, and the offence affects generations of one's family. Our positive devotion then goes on hold, sometimes for lifetimes. — “That is the worst thing one can experience in life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:15 (auto-transcript): “That is the worst thing one can experience in life. Better than one is stuck with atomic bomb. One is burnt by fire. Hundred times better. Than to be abandoned by Vashnavus. One does not suffer alone. Generations of our family members will participate in that offense. Mad…”

Aparadha often begins by associating with non-devotees. That does not mean locking ourselves in a room; we go out to give association, not to take on others' nature.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:57 (auto-transcript): “This does not mean we should cluster ourselves or be averse to the general public. No, we cannot just keep ourselves locked up in the room because we don't want to. No, we have to go and keep... Association means that we are taking their own nature. We are taking their…”

Some go to another sadhu because he speaks on confidential pastimes and think him superior to their guru. Does hearing that make one a rasika? We need to check our qualification and where we stand.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:37 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Dada Sadhu there is speaking about the learning past times. Therefore, it's superior to my guru. Yes, I should go and hear. So if you go and hear, does that mean that now you have become a true devotee? You are now a rassika bhakta? It's a qualification. It's a…”
The Bhagavatam says that faithful hearing of Krishna's pastimes with the gopis cures the heart disease of lust. Maharaj asks: are we really hearing, or getting stimulated?

We are social beings made to associate; the only choice is the quality. Without a taste for Krishna-sanga we will have asat-sanga, and even among devotees we should select those who help our practice rather than those busy criticizing. — “We cannot do without association.”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:36 (auto-transcript): “Yes, we must associate. We must associate. The quality of the association matters. But for association, we must have. We cannot do without association. We are made for that. To associate. So now it depends on the taste we have. If you don't have taste for Krishna, Krishna,…”

We are pleasure-seeking by nature and need to feel valued and loved. If we do not find that among devotees, in time we will find the association of materialists.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:14 (auto-transcript): “We'll find the association of materialists. And we can also judge ourselves and see where we are by how we value Sadhu Sangha in contrast to valuing Sadhu Sangha. If our taste for associating with the wish is increasing, I mean, if you're making advancement, and if our taste…”

Our taste for sadhu-sanga against asat-sanga shows where we stand. The nectar among devotees is not lacking — it is an ocean in full flow — so why are we not getting it?

🎙 Maharaj at 50:15 (auto-transcript): “things as they say if we are not feeling happy satisfied feeling protected feeling loved and getting love and mostly why we're not getting does that mean that this doesn't exist here it is in full swing ocean ocean of nectar is flowing ocean not a river in the ocean our…”

Krishna says four kinds of people approach him — for wealth, out of distress, from inquisitiveness and for knowledge. All of them are in the movement, so we must find those who want only to talk and hear about Krishna.

Devotees take pleasure in talking about Krishna among themselves; look at their smiling faces — that bliss is contagious. If we are not tasting it, we should check ourselves and plug back into the river of nectar.

Saying 'I love you' means nothing by itself; love is measured by consciousness and behaviour — kind words, defusing conflict, offering help. — “The actions should speak, not the words.”

🎙 Maharaj at 54:50 (auto-transcript): “I believe I love you. I believe I'm fully convinced that I love you. And then what? So what? Do you need to tell me like that? Yeah, actions should speak. The actions should speak, not the words. As spiritual warriors, we must learn to be available at all times and in all…”

In Vrindavan in 2003 a godbrother lay sick for two weeks and no one asked how he was; even his department head was slow to take him to hospital. Maharaj spent the night with him there. When he recovered he left and married, reasoning that at least a wife would not leave him alone like that.

Nobody tell him, Babu, how are you? Nobody. After two weeks, even his own the head, the…”

Many leave not because anything is wrong with Krishna, the Holy Name or scripture, but from their own weakness — and our uncaring behaviour facilitates it. Have we confused detachment with neglect?

🎙 Maharaj at 58:58 (auto-transcript): “and I'm sure there's so many other experiences many people who love the woman, devotees who are living they're not living not because Christ are not God not because something wrong with the Holy Name not because something wrong with our scripture they're living because One,…”

In breakout groups devotees reflect on sincerity without duplicity, learning how others receive love, not leaving to Krishna the care he wants us to give, and extending care beyond our own circle — a guest left without prasada all day vowed never to return.

Hare Krishna, Gurudev, again. so it was a very nice exercise everyone contributed so our reflections are the first point is that we need to be very sincere when we are dealing with other devotees so our actions must be…”
When a once-dedicated devotee weakens, offences have removed the creeper's protection. It is fenced by the regulative principles and the association of pure devotees.

List your five closest relationships and see which nourish your Krishna consciousness; keep less emotional investment where needed, deepen one advanced devotee relationship this week, and pray for protection before significant interactions.

children.note:

Sincerity and being serious in our practice. the one is sincerely practicing you have a straightforward dealing straightforward sincerity and seriousness I have a straightforward dealing with the spiritual man so we get the confidence…”

In a temple long ago, Maharaj's guru, disappointed with lazy devotees, ordered them transferred. children.topic: Q4 · Offences made as a neophyte?
children.note:

🎙 Maharaj at 117:50 (auto-transcript): “but Shrila Gurudev when we are on a very neophyte stage we don't know how to deal with the spiritual master so many offenses we commit so then how we will be like, how it will be taken care of? Neophyte devotees should not be very close. That's our tradition. Neophyte…”

By tradition neophytes serve from a distance until they mature — one does not give a child a knife. Offences from weakness are overlooked like a child wetting the floor; only premeditated offence is devastating.

🎙 Maharaj at 118:09 (auto-transcript): “Neophyte devotees should not be very close. That's our tradition. Neophyte devotees should not be very close because it's very dangerous. They should serve from distance in the beginning until they gradually become mature. Then they can come closer. Just like you don't give a…”

children.topic: Q5 · Why are devotees less caring?
children.note:
Devotees often seem impersonal and unhelpful, while non-practising family members readily help. Is this too much detachment?

🎙 Maharaj at 123:51 (auto-transcript): “what we read today has been bothering me from quite some time actually we say every morning that devotees are the ocean of compassion but in my experience it has been somewhat contrary of late because anytime i uh expect any little help even from devotees not for my personal…”

It is not detachment — Rupa Gosvami would never neglect anyone. It is hard-heartedness: practice that is only show does not melt the heart. We must become human beings first, with human qualities, before we can be devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 125:30 (auto-transcript): “no it is not it is not a detachment yes Maharaj The Rupa Goswami will not do like what we are talking. The Rupa Goswami will not neglect, will not do help. Or the Sikhs will say, will not. So when we talk about devotees, you understand. When we say devotees, we are looking at…”

children.topic: Become what you want to see
children.note:
Recruited from this world, we are still raw and being groomed. Instead of expecting the majority to behave well, emulate the behaviour you wish to see; out of thousands very few are truly devotees. — “It's not so easy to become a devotee.”

🎙 Maharaj at 131:28 (auto-transcript): “let us do it on a sign that we are few on a sign that we are few so we don't look we don't expect the majority are going to do the same thing Madhavi is telling me let me emulate that behavior I want to see in them within me at all times this is the mentality we should have…”

maps.title: Radha Sunya · Session 13 · The Many Forms of Vaishnava Aparadha

nodeData.topic: Session 13 · The Many Forms of Vaishnava Aparadha
nodeData.note: Skanda Purana · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. To fence the garden of bhakti we must know every way the mad elephant gets in: the Skanda Purana lists six Vaishnava aparadhas, down to not feeling happy on seeing a devotee and thinking ill of him in the mind. Maharaj explains how to keep standards without a destructive mindset, how to honour other religious teachers, and how Maya makes devotees fight so that both sides lose. In the questions he shows how to correct a senior indirectly and why Durga's harsh service is pure devotion. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
On the Diwali 'double celebration', Maharaj continues the series: today Vaishnava aparadha in its many forms, so that we can scrutinize every way the mad elephant can enter.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:12 (auto-transcript): “let's continue with our mission in Radha Sunya Radha Sunya Missing Missing while we are trying to understand how to overcome aparad by learning the techniques of our coming Aparada because it is a mad elephant that destroys our Bhakti Lata.”

In his village, after planting they fenced the field against four-legged animals and stood guard against birds, and they also checked the soil, the gardener's skill and the watering. Neglect any one aspect and the harvest is lost.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:35 (auto-transcript): “Remember, in a village, when we were doing farming, when we finished planting, we would fence it all around, completely. We would fence it all around. only for the animals that have four legs that can come inside. And then for the birds, we will physically stay there. We will…”

The Skanda Purana lists six offences against Vaishnavas: killing, blaspheming, not offering obeisances on seeing one, getting angry with one, not being delighted to see one, and thinking ill of one in the mind.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:13 (auto-transcript): “inside and devastate our course. Yes. Six types of Vaishnav apparatus. In the category of Vaishnav apparatus, there are six types of apparatus listed in the Skanda Purana. One, one who kills a Vaishnav. Two, one who blasphemes a Vaisnava. Three, one who upon seeing a Vaisnava…”

We may embrace a visiting devotee, welcome him and show him a room, while inwardly wondering why he came and when he will leave. That too is aparadha. — “And how long are you going to be here?”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:09 (auto-transcript): “Even though one may have offered obeisances to the Vaisnava, and they hug each other. Oh, Prabhu, Prabhu, you're welcome, you're welcome. But in the mind, I'm thinking, but why have you come? What? And how long are you going to be here? How long are you going to be here? In…”

children.topic: Even a grudge is an offence
children.note:
There is a gradation — murder and blasphemy are obviously grave — but holding a grudge or anger toward a Vaishnava is also counted as an offence.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:52 (auto-transcript): “Why? Why? Of course, we are not thinking about a devotee who is going about polluting other people's wives and stealing tents in the temple or beating, fighting devotees. We're not talking about this. We're not keeping quiet that, oh, it's a voiceover. It's a voiceover. He's…”

The 'devotee in the shower' principle does not cover someone who keeps stealing, fighting devotees or polluting others' wives.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:02 (auto-transcript): “Of course, we are not thinking about a devotee who is going about polluting other people's wives and stealing tents in the temple or beating, fighting devotees. We're not talking about this. We're not keeping quiet that, oh, it's a voiceover. It's a voiceover. He's in the…”

A devotee asked whether it is right that others stay quiet while someone keeps doing wrong. Maharaj says no: silence there means we don't care for him. When a devotee is destroying the community and discouraging others, a leader must act.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:37 (auto-transcript): “Yesterday, a devotee called me from Dallas, Dallas Temple in the U.S., and she was telling me, when a devotee is constantly doing something and people are keeping quiet about it, do something wrong, stealing, breaking things and other people are keeping quiet. So it's…”

A devotee sincerely working on himself who makes mistakes needs our prayer, teaching and correction, not anger. Holding grudges against such a Vaishnava puts our own devotional life at risk.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:05 (auto-transcript): “but if it is not like this a devotee is trying sincerely working on himself or herself and he makes mistakes we should not break our head for that, to pray for that devotee, and we should not be very angry with such a person, he don't vote because you do not help the person,…”

If someone wrongs us and we offend him in return, we are on the same level. Act so that the other person is helped and promoted, and Krishna will promote us.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:37 (auto-transcript): “And in the process of trying to look at your face, if somebody has done to us, we should not also offend the person. Otherwise, we will be on the same level. a person has done something wrong we should not allow the wrong thing the person did to also bring us down we should…”

A friend of Maharaj said we should not let the system make us break the law. Staying different is what makes the difference; someone higher is needed to help those who are low. — “Who is going to help who?”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:33 (auto-transcript): “friends said We should not allow the system to make us break the law. Someone is doing something wrong. We should not also contribute to that wrong thing. Someone has done something wrong. Someone has offended us. We should not also offend that person. Yes. At least we should…”

Not 'there he goes again', but appreciation that this soul has come to Mahaprabhu's shelter. Offer free food and shelter to disabled people in exchange for chanting and few will come — so wanting Krishna consciousness is a great fortune.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:59 (auto-transcript): “If we go to disabled people, if you go to disabled people, they are deformed in various ways and tell them, all of you should come to my place. I will feed you free. I will give you free shelter. I will feed you free, but you stay with me. I will be chanting at a place every…”

Maharaj cites the Gita: some take up devotional service without accepting Krishna as the Absolute Truth, and their efforts are defeated. Be lenient and supportive with the sincere, and carefully avoid those who have not come for Krishna.

As Bhaktivinoda Thakura's song says, we see the neophyte, intermediate and advanced devotee and learn to live with each. Rupa Gosvami and our acaryas have given every principle; we simply have to follow.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:36 (auto-transcript): “It's like, that's what I could have mentioned. I will see three devotees, the Neofi, the Madhyam, and the Hutam. Bhakti Muthukura mentioned that. We should see three people here and know how to live with all of them. Rupa Goswami gave details about the nature of devotion,…”

Jesus and Muhammad are servants of God who taught bona fide religion; we honour them personally even if we don't follow their systems. Lord Siva appeared as Sankaracarya and Buddha is glorified by Jayadeva, yet neither is on our altar.

🎙 Maharaj at 43:27 (auto-transcript): “Honoring other religious teachers. Sometimes devotees offend Jesus or offend Muhammad, but they are also servants of God, teaching bona fide systems of religion. Even though we do not celebrate their system in all respects, we honor them personally. We remember that Lord…”

Srila Prabhupada told seminarians in Australia that Jesus is our spiritual master too. Many of us came through him; he got people to accept that there is God, so we respect him without embracing everything now taught in his name.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:20 (auto-transcript): “The Prabhupada told the seminarians in Australia that we have saved Jesus as our spiritual master. We don't follow his teaching, but he did something. Some of us, we came from him. From there, we got the promotion to come here. And Jesus himself is a disciple of the…”

Remove the kindergarten and college and who will reach the university? Other traditions prepare people, so we don't blaspheme them — though some stop there out of ego when it is time to move on.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:22 (auto-transcript): “We don't go out of blaspheming other traditions. They are general brothers, but we don't condemn them. We don't follow that. We don't condemn them. Just like if we remove a kindergarten, remove college, so how do people come to university? How do people come to university? So…”

Maya's trick is to inspire those leaving her influence to fight each other, so that they gradually fall back into her grip.

🎙 Maharaj at 47:22 (auto-transcript): “Going internal through reflections. This one will have 10 minutes. Maya's fighting starting. What can easily happen is that Maya will play an interesting trick. She inspires those who are trying to leave her sphere of influence to start fighting, so that gradually they fall…”

In an argument we never think Maya is using us; we only want to prove the other wrong. The Gosvamis could easily have out-argued anyone, but did not waste time on debate whose only aim is to defeat. — “It's false ego.”

🎙 Maharaj at 47:53 (auto-transcript): “This is a very, very powerful thing, because when I'm having some argument with misunderstanding with somebody, I don't think that Maya is using us. I think that I'm right. We don't remember that somebody is putting us together to have this argument. We don't think like that.…”

When a case was raised to remove a central deity of the sampradaya from worship, an acarya went alone and defeated an 'ocean' of Vedantists. One pure devotee is the majority; Maharaj adds an acarya's joke that we have more heads than Brahma — the heads of all our acaryas.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:28 (auto-transcript): “This is how our Vajma Acharya behave. Like, he went to Chaliputu to defend me. They have a very tangible case presented to neutify, to nullify, to completely close, remove the most essential aspect of baptism, material design, who is the personification of bhakti was not…”

Krishna kills each demon once, but extinguishes the forest fire twice; acaryas explain the fire as quarrelling among Vaishnavas. When elephants fight the ground suffers, and when Vaishnavas — the light of the world — fight, the whole world suffers. — “Vaisnavas should not quarrel.”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:35 (auto-transcript): “when we look at the Bhagavatam you see Krista extinguishes fire two times there's no person Krista plays two times all the killing of demons is one, so don't say I will kill two times this demon Bakasura we're killing two times but extinguishing fire was two times the demon…”

Pick up your beads right after quarrelling with all your energy and you cannot really chant; mantras then have no effect. That is why deity worship begins with sipping water for purification.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:27 (auto-transcript): “Yes, when we are fighting, right? You notice, notice very carefully, when I'm very angry, take a beat and see if you will chant. You will chant. After just quarreling now with all of your energy, and then next when you carry a beat, you would never chant. That is how…”

No one can hold fire and be peaceful; those who hold grudges and never forgive cannot be happy.

🎙 Maharaj at 56:04 (auto-transcript): “spiritual life my god they will explain that holding grudges against devotees like holding fire no one can hold fire and be peaceful so a person cannot hold fire and be peaceful so people who are begrudging cannot be peaceful cannot be happy because we're holding fire people…”

Breakout groups reflect on being drawn into conflict, what we lose by winning arguments, and how grudges affect us.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:36 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, dear Guru Dev. Hare Krishna, dear devotees. Hare Krishna. Please accept my humble obeisance excluded. Thank you. So we have these points shared very nicely by the devotees. So first we talked about how going through a lot of personal challenges makes it…”

Devotees share that winning arguments loses the chance to connect, that grudges carried for months block chanting, that strong sadhana and remembering the guru keep one out of conflict, and that seeking forgiveness makes the heart light. Maharaj agrees that argument takes away our chanting.

🎙 Maharaj at 75:24 (auto-transcript): “encounter these challenges when we win arguments we are not actually winning we're losing the opportunity to connect deeper with those devotees and holding grudges will completely undermine any of our true efforts for advancement because we will lose the appreciation and also…”

In a fight even the winner ends up with a black eye and torn clothes; both lose spiritual strength while Maya rejoices that her opponents are distracted. Only the one who consciously avoids the fight wins, and helps others win too. — “So nobody actually wins.”

🎙 Maharaj at 87:47 (auto-transcript): “Both parties lose in fighting. It means that both parties will begin to lose some of their spiritual strength to have spiritual credits. It is so typical of fighting. Someone may win the fight, but both individuals have dirty clothes, black eyes, torn dresses, torn shirts, or…”

Whether neophyte, intermediate or advanced, anyone chanting the Holy Name should make us happy. In a place with no devotees, meeting even a neophyte makes a huge difference; among billions, here is someone honouring Krishna. — “You will be very, very happy to see such a person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 90:37 (auto-transcript): “And especially if you had gone to an environment where there's no devotee there, and the only person you meet there is a canister devotee, you will see a huge difference in your life. You see a huge difference. What it means to be a devotee. Forget about the situation. You…”

The contemplation asks us to see every devotee as part of Mahaprabhu's army, list our grudges and consciously release one person from blame each week, and ask about a devotee who doesn't delight us: among billions this person chants Krishna's name — why am I not happy?

🎙 Maharaj at 93:12 (auto-transcript): “Realization through contemplation. Continue your 30-day notebook practice with today's focus on transforming our vision of devotees. When meeting any devotee, remember, maybe they may seem difficult to deal with, but they are part of the Titanius, I mean, nonetheless.…”

Questions on a senior speaking disrespectfully, Maya Devi's role, harsh managers, and staying unprovoked.

🎙 Maharaj at 96:05 (auto-transcript): “We now have a few quick questions. and devotees who want any of the questions to be addressed please raise your hands we'll quickly begin with Shivani Mataji for our first question could you please, Anil? Hi Krishna Maharaj, physics of my most humble of your senses Maharaj, I…”

A senior devotee spoke disrespectfully about another devotee; as a junior, what should one do?

🎙 Maharaj at 96:35 (auto-transcript): “first is one day I was with one of the senior Mataji and she was explaining some subject matter to me very lovingly and she took the example of one of the devotees and with that devotee her language was not so good it was not so respectful and I felt really bad but I was…”

Krishna placed you there for a purpose; seniors often have no one to correct them and behave differently in private. As a new devotee, ask how devotees should deal with one another — a thoughtful person will reflect and change, and may later thank you. — “You can put it as a question to the person.”

🎙 Maharaj at 97:32 (auto-transcript): “I feel that Krishna has brought you in another time for a purpose. Because this senior person may not have somebody senior to encourage her. And they may not see what it is they're doing because when we are not with our senior, we behave differently. So in the public, people…”

Krishna puts us in every situation for a purpose, and being Krishna conscious means trying to learn that purpose.

🎙 Maharaj at 101:01 (auto-transcript): “Yes, Krishna put us in every situation for purpose. And we should try to learn that purpose. That is what it means to be Krishna conscious. To be conscious of Krishna all the time. All right? Yes, Maya. Thank you so much. My second question is, why Maya Devi feels happy if we…”

children.topic: Q2 · Why is Maya happy when we fight?
children.note:
If Maya Devi serves Krishna, why would she be happy at our quarrels?

🎙 Maharaj at 101:25 (auto-transcript): “My second question is, why Maya Devi feels happy if we are going younger? She is also serving Krishna. Yes. Maya Devi is a devotee of Krishna pure devotee of Krishna not a conditioned soul she's a pure devotee of Krishna if you if you when you go to Mayapu you see Samanti…”

Maya Devi is a pure devotee. She asked Krishna to change her service of harassing souls and he refused, saying only she can do it; as Subhadra she removes the miseries she gives as Durga. She takes no pleasure in suffering — she simply lets no contaminated soul disturb her master.

🎙 Maharaj at 101:36 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Maya Devi is a devotee of Krishna pure devotee of Krishna not a conditioned soul she's a pure devotee of Krishna if you if you when you go to Mayapu you see Samanti Devi sitting there with Theta Mahatma I see Druga she had approached Krishna but my lord the service you…”

children.topic: Q3 · Managers who feel entitled to be harsh
children.note:
Mahaprabhu was sometimes strict, but his followers were forgiving with each other; why do devotees in positions feel entitled to be rude?

🎙 Maharaj at 104:52 (auto-transcript): “I would like to ask Gurudev about because we what I could understand And what I was able to understand from this Radha Shunya seminar and all your lectures, all these years, is actually that a mature Vaishnava or a Vaishnava practitioner, mature in any, the equivalent of his…”

Rich and renounced, from every background, Mahaprabhu's associates blended perfectly without argument, to set a standard for us.

🎙 Maharaj at 110:23 (auto-transcript): “yes definitely that's the nature of the first of us that uh we've seen they are together they are all individuals or all individuals from also different backgrounds and wealthy and strict renunciate. They all mix up together. But they blended perfectly. There is no…”

A brahmana insulted Haridasa Thakura over loud chanting; Haridasa humbly quoted scripture and felt nothing. The offender soon suffered a terrible disease. Purity does not drive people away by defeating them; it attracts them to take the Holy Name.

🎙 Maharaj at 111:53 (auto-transcript): “We see how Heridas Akwe was insulted. Koppal Chapa. Hey, Heridas! I can see that now you're becoming a scholar. Who taught you this? if what you're saying is not correct because you talk about in the process the response is oh we are talking about me I'm nobody what I can say…”

Sometimes I react from inside and later repent; how can I stay steady?

🎙 Maharaj at 116:00 (auto-transcript): “Shri Gurdwyer I have one I have one question what happens to me that sometimes if I have some argument with anyone sometimes there is no provoking situation from the heart at that time external factors don't affect me but sometimes it affects me and at that time I see that…”

With strong sadhana, like a strong immune system, nothing in the environment affects us and we can face anything happily. — “If your immune system is very strong, you won't be affected by anything.”

🎙 Maharaj at 117:13 (auto-transcript): “If your immune system is very strong, you won't be affected by anything. Just like if your immune system is very strong, you won't have any difficulty with any disease that comes in the environment. Every disease that comes in the environment will not affect you. The person…”

nodeData.topic: Session 14 · Authentic and Inauthentic Service
nodeData.note: SB 1.1.2 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Every field has genuine and counterfeit practitioners, and so does religion: the Bhagavatam throws out cheating religion, and the acaryas give prema only to the sincere. Maharaj shows how aparadha opens the door to adharma and speculation, how to take the Holy Name as medicine in the right dose, and — voicing the ego's honest answers — asks whom we are really serving when we chant, lead kirtan or give class. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Halfway through the series, Maharaj turns to authentic and inauthentic methods of service: service that is genuinely devotional, and service that is mechanical.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:29 (auto-transcript): “Radha Suniya, Missing Mercy, day 14, we have been trying to understand how dangerous a parada is so that we can work out our ways to overcome it. by the mercy of our chariots. So today we are focusing on authentic and inauthentic methods of service. Service, which is bona…”

children.topic: Not everything we do is bhakti
children.note:
We should look carefully at what our interest in Krishna consciousness is, because not everything done in Krishna consciousness is devotional service.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:56 (auto-transcript): “So we should try to carefully look at what is our interest in Christian consciousness. Because it is not everything we do in Christian consciousness that is devotional service. This we have mentioned many times. There are certain practices that encourage healthy goods,…”

Alongside genuine currency, lawyers and doctors there are counterfeits — irresponsible people who accept no accountability. Maharaj sees it everywhere: in companies, in the market and in spiritual circles, where common people go easily to the frauds.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:25 (auto-transcript): “genuine with fraudulent practitioners, genuine with fraudulent practitioners. In most endeavors, there are authentic methods and inauthentic methods that are bogus, counterfeit, or hypocritical. We know that there is genuine currency, but there is also counterfeit currency.”

One teacher tells a crowd to take whatever mantra they feel comfortable with and tell no one — that will take them back to Godhead. There is no connection between such a guru and disciple.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:21 (auto-transcript): “Someone is telling, all of you look at the screen, any mantra that you feel comfortable with, take that. That is your mantra, but don't tell somebody else. That is your guide to the mantra. It will take you back home, back to Godhead. What we have experienced is that the…”

In Maharaj's experience disciples advance quickly because the spiritual master influences them, as Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati and Srila Prabhupada did. Without that connection, how can one advance? We need support to succeed.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:41 (auto-transcript): “What we have experienced is that the spiritual master has influence on the disciples. And that's what makes the disciples to make rapid advancement. Yes, the Ramonian had. The Bhakti Dhanthas also had influence on him. He had influence on his disciples. Slapopar has influence…”

When a devotee chants carefully, serves meticulously to please the acaryas and guru, and studies scripture to enter its mysteries, the acaryas, Krishna and the Holy Name take notice and give the support needed — and they also notice the opposite.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:40 (auto-transcript): “When a devotee is sincerely and seriously engaged in carefully trying the holiness of a Christian loudly and distinctly, and with the mind, with the aim, with the interest to attire a Christian's And one is also meticulously doing his or her service for that purpose, just to…”

Gour Govinda Swami stressed the difference between the guileless and the duplicitous. The sincere, whose interest is one with Krishna's, receive prema; the duplicitous may get facilities and positions, but a bona fide acarya cheats the cheaters by never giving them prema. — “They will succeed.”

🎙 Maharaj at 23:52 (auto-transcript): “Slagov Guvina Maharas always emphasizes on Niskapot Bogta and Sarkapot Bogta. Niskapot, he said that they will get all the necessary support in a Christian consciousness because they are sincere, they are genuine, they are genuine. Their interest is one with Christian's…”
The irresolute have many-branched desires; a Krishna conscious person wants only one thing, and that one thing includes everything. — “That is Krishna.”

Devotees should be responsible and accountable, regularly measuring their Krishna consciousness to know where they are and where they are going; bogus practitioners stay baffled and frustrated.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:50 (auto-transcript): “Devotives should be responsible, accountable in our activities. We have really discussed how to measure our Christian consciousness in our previous discussion. In this way, we can know where we are, where we are going, and how we are going. It is very important. Yes. Those…”

The Bhagavatam's opening verses reject all materially motivated, cheating religion; its message is for devotees free from envy and duplicity. Misused religion creates havoc, fragmentation and division.

Many demons take shelter of religion, and people get more discouraged in religious places than in factories. A policeman in Mathura told a disciple that all religious people are cheaters — untrue, but when ninety in a hundred cheat, people conclude so. — “that is not true”

🎙 Maharaj at 30:48 (auto-transcript): “some years ago when a policeman in Matura he was telling one one disciple he was telling one disciple I don't believe all these religious people I don't believe them all of them are cheaters that is not true that is not true But if you have 100 over 10, it will mean like…”

The Gita describes the ignorant, the faithless and the doubter. Much doubt comes from what people heard from religious organisations; cheated again and again, they decide all are the same, and the cheaters make the bona fide preachers' work very hard.

Much church growth comes from disagreement: 'the money isn't shared, the place runs because of me, I'll start my own' — hence Apostolic 1, 2, 3 and so on.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:51 (auto-transcript): “fundamentations, divisions. This is how Christianity is expanding. They're not expanding on the healthy ground. They are spending based on disagreement. I don't agree with you. After we sat together for some years and we are not sharing the money together, I'm not getting the…”

A bona fide organisation expands in joy: we have grown to a hundred, so let's open another branch. — “That is healthy expansion.”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:01 (auto-transcript): “Which is different from a bona fide organization expanding into joy. Expanding because we are increasing in number. So we are expanding. So now we are 100. Let's start with another branch. That is healthy. That is healthy expansion. Yes. And we should expand in that way. All…”

children.topic: A ticket to the right destination
children.note: Paying for a mantra and doing whatever you like, or chanting a demigod's mantra, takes you to that demigod, not to Krishna. An airline checks that your ticket from Lagos matches your plane; how can we expect to go anywhere we like spiritually?

children.topic: The right thing for the wrong reason
children.note:
Reflecting on a devotee who prepares a talk but secretly craves praise, Maharaj says service becoming self-service in disguise happens daily, and that mistaking recognition for realisation is common among us. — “doing something wrong is better than doing the right thing”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:31 (auto-transcript): “why not it is happening daily what's harder doing something wrong or doing the right thing for the wrong reason doing something wrong is better than doing the right thing for the wrong reason. It's more dangerous. Have I mistaken spiritual recognition for spiritual…”

Before the breakout groups, Maharaj asks that no one dominate: Caitanya Mahaprabhu said an eloquent speaker speaks concisely.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:39 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna. So we're starting the rooms. Also one person you know dominate the whole time and that you don't have one minute to speak. You should be careful to speak appropriately, concisely. Because Chita Mbam Puh Maha Chita Chita Mbam Puh Maha said that is eloquent…”

nodeData.topic: Session 15 · Offending the Holy Dham
nodeData.note: Padma Purana · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The holy dhama is as worshipable as Krishna, but it reveals itself only to those who enter in the right mood, as Akrura and Jiva Gosvami did, and the first dhama offence is to offend the guru who holds its key. Because the dhama amplifies both devotion and offence, Maharaj warns against tourism, business and familiarity there, and gives a simple remedy: be compassionate, humble, appreciative and grateful. In the questions he explains why the dhama stays hidden — offences, weak conviction and lack of faith. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Entering the dham in the right mood
children.note:
Today's theme is offending the holy dhama. Places of pilgrimage are charged with the pastimes of the Lord and his devotees; Vrindavan and Mayapur are replicas of the spiritual world, as worshipable as Krishna, and one who truly enters feels Krishna's presence at once.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:48 (auto-transcript): “So today, in particular, we are looking at offending the holy dam. How to avoid offending the holy dam so that we can get purified. Yes. Tirita Apparat and Dam Apparat Offenses in Sacred Places Tirita Apparat or Dam Apparat are offenses that one may commit when visiting…”

We should go to Gopisvara Mahadeva for entrance into Vrindavan and prepare our consciousness before we go; otherwise we only see India. — “We are going to see India, not Brindavan.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:10 (auto-transcript): “That is when we have entered Brindavan. Therefore, it is recommended that we must go to Gupishwara Mahadev to give us entrance into Brindavan. Without that, we are not going to be in Brindavan. We are going to see India, not Brindavan.”

Sent by Kamsa, Akrura knew Krishna and Balarama would kill Kamsa and bring peace, and all the way he thought only of his fortune in seeing Krishna. At Vrindavan's border he saw Krishna's footprints, jumped from the chariot and rolled in the dust.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:56 (auto-transcript): “Like Akura. Akura was thinking, although Kamsa has sent for Christian Balaran, but he had evil intention. His intention is to kill these two boys. But I know Christian Balaran had a supreme position of Godhead and the Kamsa would not be able to kill them. Therefore, Akura…”
Uddhava, though very exalted, offers obeisances not to the gopis but to the dust of their feet. That is the mood for entering holy places.

Jiva Gosvami entered Mayapur in his mind as soon as he left home, meditating on Nityananda Prabhu. Nityananda sent people to find him, and they recognised him by the ecstatic symptoms that made him fall unconscious. They had communicated by a 'transcendental cell phone' — Maharaj jokes that ordinary cell phones are for degraded people.

🎙 Maharaj at 26:02 (auto-transcript): “And in the case of Sr. Javagoswami, I will have the fortune to see the Balaram, Lord Nityananda Balaram, and he will give me mercy. He will reveal the dam to me. He will give me the vision to see Mayapu, and I will see all the associated with Tita Mahaprabhu, and I will…”

Nityananda Prabhu took Jiva first for blessings and then to Srivasa Angana, where he showed him Mahaprabhu's kirtan party with Nityananda himself dancing in it; Jiva fell unconscious a second time. We should pray like that when we go to Mayapur.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:03 (auto-transcript): “Nityanana Prabhu revealed the dam to Jiva Goswami. Nityanana Prabhu, he took Jiva Goswami to Jopi to get blessings at the beginning. And then from there, he went to Srivastangam. In Srivastangam, he brought Lord Chita Mahavu's Harinam party, right? He brought the whole…”

children.topic: First dham offence: offending the guru
children.note:
Like the ten offences to the Holy Name, there are ten offences to the dhama. Asked which comes first, Maharaj explains it is to offend the guru who reveals the dhama — he holds the key to Goloka.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:37 (auto-transcript): “For people to do the ones who be careful of Dham Apparat. They have been enumerated as 10 also. We have 10 for the Holy Name. We should have 10 for the Dham. And the first one is what? What is the first one? What is the first one to be avoided? The first Dham Apparat. Very,…”

One can live physically in Mayapur, Vrindavan or Jagannatha Puri and still not be counted as living there, because aparadha covers the real dhama from us. — “Aparada will throw us out,”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:06 (auto-transcript): “We can never enter the Nava. We can even live there physically. You can live in Mayapur. You can live in Nava physically. You can live in Jaganapuri physically. But one is not considered to live there, to be living there because of Aparada. Aparada will throw us out, will…”

The dhama is the holy place; within it, tirthas are the particular spots where Krishna or his pure devotees performed pastimes, which is why we go from place to place even inside Vrindavan.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:45 (auto-transcript): “The Dham and the Tiritha. You understand? The Dham is a holy place. That's a holy place, the Dham. What Tiritha? within the holy place what is this dam, the holy place like in Brindavan, why do we have to go from one place to another place to another place we are already in…”

Srila Prabhupada created tirthas outside Vrindavan, Mayapur and Puri, because a pure devotee performed his pastimes there for the devotees.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:19 (auto-transcript): “Shira Prabhupada has created Tirita outside Vendavan outside Maipu outside Jagadana Puri so those places are what? Tirita because the Lord the Lord's pure devotee has performed a passing in these places for the devotees Therefore, they have become exalted places. So the…”

Scripture recommends pilgrimage so that we may meet holy people there and question them. Reading about a place in a book is not the same as hearing from a sadhu; only by a pure devotee's mercy can we enter the mystery.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:45 (auto-transcript): “So the scripture recommends that we should visit these places. Why? Because when we visit these places, we may have the fortune to get in some places where the holy people are staying there. Or some are visiting there. We will have the fortune to meet them there and question…”

Some 'spend Kartik in Vrindavan' taking pictures and eating, even onions, garlic and meat. Is that Vrindavan?

🎙 Maharaj at 36:08 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, the scripture of the Kermitra should go to this place and not go and just see, take pictures and eat and then go back to the house. Where are you coming from? I'm coming from Braindavan Dam. Oh, great. In the month of Karthik, I spent the whole month in Braindavan.…”

Maharaj asks devotees now in Vrindavan to go and pray to Gopisvara Mahadeva every Monday, so that their Kartik becomes more meaningful.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:20 (auto-transcript): “So dear devotees, all of you who are there in Brandavan, please all of you who are there in Brindam every Monday please go to Mahathir go and pray to him all of you are fortunate to be there now please go every Monday whatever you are doing on Monday you should go there and…”

Pilgrimage brings freedom from material bondage, but that is only a ticket; the goal is to be engaged in the Lord's personal service, which is easily attained by one who lives in Mathura-mandala even for a moment.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:07 (auto-transcript): “yes? The eye that see God shall die. To travel to different places of forgiveness means what? To attain emancipation from material bondage. That is visiting holy places. This, however, is not the highest professional stage. After attaining this liberated stage, Brahma Buddha,…”

One fixed in devotional service, thinking of Radha and Krishna wherever he is, lives in Vrindavan; one who stays there physically with his consciousness outside does not.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:09 (auto-transcript): “This is the meaning of being fortunate that one has certain Unfortunately, one will get the blessing to enter into the mysteries of devotional service, your devotional service, Krishna consciousness. Then, such a person is considered to be staying in Mathura Mandala. Either…”

A friend visiting Mayapur was asked by a resident for his contact so that the resident's son could work abroad and come back to build houses in Mayapur and collect rent. Is that living in the dhama, or business?

🎙 Maharaj at 41:56 (auto-transcript): “A friend was telling me he visited Mayapu. He visited Mayapu. And then another devotee who was there said, Oh, Prabhu, oh, Prabhu, oh, you see, how can I get your contact when you're communicating with you? because I want my son when my son finishes from the I want my son to…”

Gokula is superior to Vaikuntha: Vaikuntha has nothing like Krishna's pastimes, his countless gopis, or a mother coming with a stick to beat him as a butter thief. Krishna is the reservoir of irregularities — even Vrindavan's houses are not straight, while Delhi's are.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:04 (auto-transcript): “Gokul Brindavan is what? superior to Baikuntha. Can you imagine that? Why? Baikuntha is the spiritual world. How is it possible that this Gokul is superior to Baikuntha? Somebody asked me this question. It had me as a spoiler in the lecture. Somebody asked me, how is that…”

The dhama is revealed only to eyes anointed with the ointment of love. Asked who runs that 'factory', a devotee answers Srimati Radharani; when she anoints someone, he can see Syamasundara.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:46 (auto-transcript): “buildings. Where is the factory for Premaljana? And who is the director of that company? Who? Who is the director of this company? Please tell me who is the director of the factory? Premaljana factory? Huh? Gurudev Srimati Radarani? Yes, Srimati Radarani. Radarani is the…”

In the dhama good deeds bring a hundredfold result and so do bad ones. We come to dump our garbage there; if we make garbage there, where will we dispose of it? One answer given is that one should then never leave until freed of those reactions.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:55 (auto-transcript): “So, while we amplify or maximize our fortune by visiting the holy dam, we can also destroy it. if one makes offenses in other places we come to holy places, one gets purified but if one makes offenses in these places we may all never get purified we carry cabbages there to…”

Maharaj has seen godbrothers return from Vrindavan or Mayapur and leave the movement — some to Sai Baba — and others come back with chronic disease, because of offences in the dhama. — “This I have seen with my own eyes.”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:11 (auto-transcript): “seen some devotees who visited my school and I have some good brothers who visited. When they came back from there, they left the movement. I have, I have, practical, the God Brothers. They went to Brandavan, Mayaki, and they came back and left the movement. Some joined the…”

Krishna forgives offences of those who serve and chant the name of Radha; Rupa Gosvami says one who says 'Radha' dries up the ocean of material existence.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:06 (auto-transcript): “This morning we're hearing, Krishna forgives offenses for those who are engaged in serving the cemetery. Those who are chanting the cemetery in his name, Radha. Rupa Goswami said that. And in Vidakta Madhava, Rupa Goswami said, anyone who say Radha, the ocean of material…”

Those who vowed to chant Radha Kripa Kataksha this Kartik should add Krishna's Kripa Kataksha prayer as well; our system is Radha-Syamasundara together, and that is complete.

🎙 Maharaj at 55:44 (auto-transcript): “And those of us who are also taking vows in Kaltik to chant the Radha Kripa Kataksa. If you chant Radha Kripa Kataksa, it's good, but it's not complete. So we should not chant only Radha Kripa Kataksa. We should also chant Krishna Kripa Kataksa style, Chotram. Then it's…”

Someone serving in a holy place at first feels everything sacred; gradually familiarity sees only faults and politics. The place has not changed — what we saw at the start is still there; it is our own consciousness that has changed. Prabhupada said long-time devotees should rejoin ISKCON.

🎙 Maharaj at 58:26 (auto-transcript): “What we see in the beginning when we come to Krishna consciousness, it remains as it is. We don't see those things. It doesn't mean they are there for those who also come and do like we can. It is our own consciousness that has changed. Therefore, if we change, then we go…”

Groups suggest entering with senior devotees, hearing the dhama's glories beforehand, keeping busy in service, treating every temple as our own to clean, reciting the ten offences to the dhama, and remembering the dhama knows what we think.

🎙 Maharaj at 73:40 (auto-transcript): “we discussed that when um you're in a situation and you're in the temple and you're hearing things that you don't want to hear that krishna is testing your level to see where you're at to see how you would react to a situation in that matter and then i also shared that i've…”
Yudhisthira tells Vidura that devotees like him are holy places personified, since they carry the Lord in their hearts. So we visit holy places to hear from sadhus, not just to look around.

Roaming the dhama alone is not authorised. Our acaryas, though Vrajavasis themselves, were sent to stay under Rupa Gosvami and others, to teach us to go under a senior devotee's care.

🎙 Maharaj at 86:59 (auto-transcript): “She will help us. She will take care of us and guide us. One should not just go to the holy place in Vandam and just be around there. That is not authorized. We see all our acharyas, when they go to Vandam, they are specifically sent to go and stay with these devotees. Go and…”

Offences to the Name, the dhama, service, Vaishnavas and the guru can seem overwhelming. The key is to be compassionate, humble, appreciative and grateful for Krishna's mercy; then the Lord in the heart keeps us from offences.

🎙 Maharaj at 88:03 (auto-transcript): “Next, don't be overwhelmed. There are so many apparatus. Nam apparatus, offenses to living. Dham apparatus, offenses to the holy places. Saber apparatus, offenses that are made while rendering service. Vaishnam apparatus, offenses to devotees. And Guru apparatus, offenses to…”

Without humility and compassion it is very rare to be free of offences. The neophyte can offend anyone, anytime, especially when close to devotees, so we should raise our standard to the intermediate level. — “Because medium is safe.”

🎙 Maharaj at 89:42 (auto-transcript): “humility If you don't have compassion, it's very, very, very, very rare for a person to be free from offenses in this category. Very, very rare. We can easily make offenses. So we have been repeatedly saying that we should try to raise our standard from canister to medium.…”

The contemplation: before chanting, check compassion ('they are trying, I am trying'), humility, appreciation and gratitude ('I didn't find you, you found me'); and journal each evening where these were lost.

🎙 Maharaj at 90:32 (auto-transcript): “Realization through contemplation. Continue your 30-day notebook to raise focus on damn consciousness. Part one, before entering Monday chanting, spend 10 minutes. Five, turning your consciousness. Don't rust in. Check your heart using these four qualities. Compassionate.…”

Two questions on visiting the dhama.

🎙 Maharaj at 96:30 (auto-transcript): “we will move on to question and answers if there are any please raise your hand Gurudev we have one question in the chat box yes let's start from there ok it's from Resika Preeti Mataji she's saying had a question when visiting a holy place like Shri Dham with family or…”

Family or friends visiting a dhama sometimes criticize the atmosphere, devotees or management. How do we respond without seeming self-righteous?

🎙 Maharaj at 96:46 (auto-transcript): “she's saying had a question when visiting a holy place like Shri Dham with family or friends we sometimes find that others may unknowingly criticize the atmosphere devotees or management there Such words can feel deeply disturbing to us. How can we conduct ourselves in these…”

Prepare people's consciousness before taking them. It is said everyone in Jagannatha Puri has four arms, yet we see people spitting tobacco and pandas pulling at shirts; the dhama is covered and reveals itself only by the mercy of its residents and protectors such as Lord Siva.

🎙 Maharaj at 97:23 (auto-transcript): “Before we take people to the Dham, it is good to prepare the consciousness. we are going to Mayapur, we are going to Dharm, we are going to Jagannathpuri Dondavan Dasakura said Jagannathpuri, everyone has four hands that is but when we get today we don't see people with four…”

With faith, full conviction and freedom from offences the acaryas can reveal the dhama. Politely tell critics not to judge, and follow Prabhupada's advice that those not yet mature stay no more than three days in Vrindavan.

🎙 Maharaj at 106:36 (auto-transcript): “Yeah, so we groom the devotees we are taking for the dam so that they have a better understanding where we are going and what to expect. So, yeah, we need to be free from expenses. We need to have faith. We should believe that what the scripture says is true, what our child…”

children.topic: Q2 · Why isn't the dham revealed?
children.note:
Most devotees are careful not to offend the guru, so why is the dhama not revealed to everyone?

🎙 Maharaj at 109:05 (auto-transcript): “There is one more question from Kamala Kshimata Ji. She's saying, Hare Krishna Gurudev. Gurudev, as you're told, that first offense to the holy dham is offending guru. So Gurudev in general, all devotees are very careful to offend Gurudev, either in Dham or outside. So then…”

Many visit Loi Bazaar and Banke Bihari and come to their guru only on the last day — is that respect? Minimizing the guru's disciples is also guru-aparadha, since he is connected with them.

🎙 Maharaj at 109:40 (auto-transcript): “We should be free from offenses. How many of us are free from offenses? to be free from offenses not only to the good and also I'm not sure that everyone is free from offending I'm not sure either we're doing it mentally or grossly we talk behind or disrespectful many people…”

Jiva Gosvami arrived full of Nityananda consciousness and everything was revealed. If it is not happening to us, we are not free from offences and lack faith.

🎙 Maharaj at 111:57 (auto-transcript): “We just mentioned that Srila Jeeva Goswami, he was coming full of Netanyahu consciousness, full of Mahapu consciousness. He prepared, and exactly when he got it there, that's what happened. That means he's free from offenses. If we are free from offenses, the same thing will…”

Maharaj asks who has never felt Krishna did not answer a prayer. When a devotee claims Krishna always answers yet admits crying easily, he sternly corrects her: one who believes in Krishna cries only from joy. He explains he raised his voice so all would understand — his guru did not leave him in ignorance. — “A person who has belief in Krishna”

nodeData.topic: Session 16 · Jahnava Devi and Women Gurus
nodeData.note: · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Answering the question 'where are the women gurus?', Maharaj shows how the material and spiritual worlds are run by feminine potencies, culminating in Srimati Radharani, and explains why the word 'less intelligent' is misunderstood. Through Jahnava Devi, who never campaigned to be a guru yet united and protected the Vaishnavas, he warns against politics and cheating religion in devotional life. In the questions he speaks on staying balanced when hurt, not meditating on others' faults, darshan with phones, a Vaishnavi's focus, and how faith grows. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
